rows.question: Please generate a summary of the closing balances at the end of each month for each customer transactions, show the monthly changes and monthly cumulative bank account balances. Ensure that even if a customer has no account activity in a given month, the balance for that month is still included in the output.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_transactions_canonicalized AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  txn_date,
  txn_amount,
  CASE
    WHEN lower(txn_type) IN ('deposit','credit') THEN 'DEPOSIT'
    WHEN lower(txn_type) IN ('withdrawal','withdraw','debit') THEN 'WITHDRAWAL'
    ELSE upper(txn_type)
  END AS txn_type_canonical,
  CASE
    WHEN lower(txn_type) IN ('deposit','credit') THEN txn_amount
    WHEN lower(txn_type) IN ('withdrawal','withdraw','debit') THEN -txn_amount
    ELSE txn_amount
  END AS signed_amount,
  CASE
    WHEN length(txn_date) BETWEEN 8 AND 10 AND instr(txn_date,'-')=0 AND instr(txn_date,'/')=0 THEN NULL
    WHEN instr(txn_date,'-')>0 THEN
      CAST(substr(txn_date,1,4) AS INTEGER)
    WHEN instr(txn_date,'/')>0 THEN
      CAST(substr(txn_date,7,4) AS INTEGER)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS txn_year,
  CASE
    WHEN instr(txn_date,'-')>0 THEN
      CAST(substr(txn_date,6,2) AS INTEGER)
    WHEN instr(txn_date,'/')>0 THEN
      CAST(substr(txn_date,4,2) AS INTEGER)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS txn_month,
  CASE
    WHEN instr(txn_date,'-')>0 THEN
      CAST(substr(txn_date,9,2) AS INTEGER)
    WHEN instr(txn_date,'/')>0 THEN
      CAST(substr(txn_date,1,2) AS INTEGER)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS txn_day
FROM customer_transactions
),
customer_transaction_monthly_agg AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  txn_year AS year,
  txn_month AS month,
  date(substr(txn_year || '-' || printf('%02d', txn_month) || '-01',1,10)) AS month_start_date,
  date(date(substr(txn_year || '-' || printf('%02d', txn_month) || '-01',1,10), '+1 month', '-1 day')) AS month_end_date,
  SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type_canonical = 'deposit' AND signed_amount IS NOT NULL THEN signed_amount ELSE 0 END) AS total_deposits,
  SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type_canonical = 'withdrawal' AND signed_amount IS NOT NULL THEN ABS(signed_amount) ELSE 0 END) AS total_withdrawals,
  SUM(COALESCE(signed_amount,0)) AS net_flow,
  COUNT(*) AS transaction_count,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(*) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS activity_flag
FROM customer_transactions_canonicalized
GROUP BY customer_id, txn_year, txn_month
),
customer_monthly_balance_windows AS (
SELECT
  m.customer_id AS customer_id,
  m.year AS year,
  m.month AS month,
  m.month_start_date AS month_start_date,
  m.month_end_date AS month_end_date,
  -- closing_balance = cumulative sum of signed transactions up to month_end (i.e., net position at month end)
  (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(ctc.signed_amount),0)
   FROM customer_transactions_canonicalized ctc
   WHERE ctc.customer_id = m.customer_id
     AND (ctc.txn_year < m.year OR (ctc.txn_year = m.year AND ctc.txn_month <= m.month))
  ) AS closing_balance,
  -- previous month's closing balance (closing balance at end of prior calendar month)
  (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(ctc2.signed_amount),0)
   FROM customer_transactions_canonicalized ctc2
   WHERE ctc2.customer_id = m.customer_id
     AND (ctc2.txn_year < CASE WHEN m.month = 1 THEN m.year ELSE m.year END
          OR (ctc2.txn_year = m.year AND ctc2.txn_month <= CASE WHEN m.month = 1 THEN 12 ELSE m.month - 1 END)
          OR (m.month = 1 AND ctc2.txn_year <= m.year - 1 AND (ctc2.txn_year < m.year OR (ctc2.txn_year = m.year AND ctc2.txn_month <= 12)))
     )
  ) AS previous_closing_balance,
  -- monthly_change = closing_balance - previous_closing_balance
  (
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(ctc.signed_amount),0)
     FROM customer_transactions_canonicalized ctc
     WHERE ctc.customer_id = m.customer_id
       AND (ctc.txn_year < m.year OR (ctc.txn_year = m.year AND ctc.txn_month <= m.month))
    )
    -
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(ctc2.signed_amount),0)
     FROM customer_transactions_canonicalized ctc2
     WHERE ctc2.customer_id = m.customer_id
       AND (ctc2.txn_year < CASE WHEN m.month = 1 THEN m.year ELSE m.year END
            OR (ctc2.txn_year = m.year AND ctc2.txn_month <= CASE WHEN m.month = 1 THEN 12 ELSE m.month - 1 END)
            OR (m.month = 1 AND ctc2.txn_year <= m.year - 1 AND (ctc2.txn_year < m.year OR (ctc2.txn_year = m.year AND ctc2.txn_month <= 12)))
       )
    )
  ) AS monthly_change,
  -- cumulative_balance identical to closing_balance (running total through month)
  (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(ctc3.signed_amount),0)
   FROM customer_transactions_canonicalized ctc3
   WHERE ctc3.customer_id = m.customer_id
     AND (ctc3.txn_year < m.year OR (ctc3.txn_year = m.year AND ctc3.txn_month <= m.month))
  ) AS cumulative_balance,
  -- activity_flag: if there were any transactions in that month per monthly aggregate
  CASE WHEN m.activity_flag IS NOT NULL THEN m.activity_flag ELSE
    (CASE WHEN EXISTS (
       SELECT 1 FROM customer_transactions_canonicalized ctc4
       WHERE ctc4.customer_id = m.customer_id
         AND ctc4.txn_year = m.year AND ctc4.txn_month = m.month
    ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
  END AS activity_flag
FROM customer_transaction_monthly_agg m
)
SELECT
  seq.customer_id,
  seq.year,
  seq.month,
  seq.month_start_date,
  seq.month_end_date,
  -- closing balance is cumulative sum of net_flow up to and including this month
  SUM(COALESCE(ma.net_flow, 0)) OVER (
    PARTITION BY seq.customer_id
    ORDER BY seq.year, seq.month
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS closing_balance,
  -- previous month's closing balance
  SUM(COALESCE(ma.net_flow, 0)) OVER (
    PARTITION BY seq.customer_id
    ORDER BY seq.year, seq.month
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
  ) AS previous_closing_balance,
  -- monthly_change = closing_balance - previous_closing_balance (NULL for first month)
  (SUM(COALESCE(ma.net_flow, 0)) OVER (
     PARTITION BY seq.customer_id
     ORDER BY seq.year, seq.month
     ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
   )
   -
   SUM(COALESCE(ma.net_flow, 0)) OVER (
     PARTITION BY seq.customer_id
     ORDER BY seq.year, seq.month
     ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
   )
  ) AS monthly_change,
  -- cumulative_balance equals closing_balance as requested
  SUM(COALESCE(ma.net_flow, 0)) OVER (
    PARTITION BY seq.customer_id
    ORDER BY seq.year, seq.month
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS cumulative_balance,
  COALESCE(ma.activity_flag, 0) AS activity_flag
FROM
  -- sequence of months per customer between their first and last txn month
  (
    SELECT
      c.customer_id,
      strftime('%Y', date(m.start_date, ('+' || (m.offset) || ' months'))) AS year,
      CAST(strftime('%m', date(m.start_date, ('+' || (m.offset) || ' months'))) AS INTEGER) AS month,
      date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(m.start_date, ('+' || (m.offset) || ' months')))) AS month_start_date,
      date(date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(m.start_date, ('+' || (m.offset) || ' months')))), '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end_date
    FROM
      (
        -- per-customer start and end month (first and last txn month)
        SELECT
          customer_id,
          date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', MIN(txn_date))) AS start_date,
          date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', MAX(txn_date))) AS end_date,
          CAST(( (strftime('%Y', MAX(txn_date)) - strftime('%Y', MIN(txn_date))) * 12
                 + (strftime('%m', MAX(txn_date)) - strftime('%m', MIN(txn_date)))
               ) AS INTEGER) AS month_span
        FROM customer_transactions
        GROUP BY customer_id
      ) c
      -- cross join a generated number series 0..month_span to expand months
      JOIN (
        SELECT 0 AS offset UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4
        UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9
        UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14
        UNION ALL SELECT 15 UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17 UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19
        UNION ALL SELECT 20 UNION ALL SELECT 21 UNION ALL SELECT 22 UNION ALL SELECT 23 UNION ALL SELECT 24
        UNION ALL SELECT 25 UNION ALL SELECT 26 UNION ALL SELECT 27 UNION ALL SELECT 28 UNION ALL SELECT 29
        UNION ALL SELECT 30 UNION ALL SELECT 31 UNION ALL SELECT 32 UNION ALL SELECT 33 UNION ALL SELECT 34
        UNION ALL SELECT 35 UNION ALL SELECT 36 UNION ALL SELECT 37 UNION ALL SELECT 38 UNION ALL SELECT 39
        UNION ALL SELECT 40 UNION ALL SELECT 41 UNION ALL SELECT 42 UNION ALL SELECT 43 UNION ALL SELECT 44
        UNION ALL SELECT 45 UNION ALL SELECT 46 UNION ALL SELECT 47 UNION ALL SELECT 48 UNION ALL SELECT 49
        UNION ALL SELECT 50 UNION ALL SELECT 51 UNION ALL SELECT 52 UNION ALL SELECT 53 UNION ALL SELECT 54
        UNION ALL SELECT 55 UNION ALL SELECT 56 UNION ALL SELECT 57 UNION ALL SELECT 58 UNION ALL SELECT 59
        UNION ALL SELECT 60
      ) m ON m.offset <= c.month_span
  ) seq
  LEFT JOIN customer_transaction_monthly_agg ma
    ON ma.customer_id = seq.customer_id
   AND ma.year = CAST(seq.year AS INTEGER)
   AND ma.month = seq.month
ORDER BY
  seq.customer_id ASC,
  seq.year ASC,
  seq.month ASC

rows.question: For each customer and each month of 2020, first calculate the month-end balance by adding all deposit amounts and subtracting all withdrawal amounts that occurred during that specific month. Then determine which month in 2020 has the highest count of customers with a positive month-end balance and which month has the lowest count. For each of these two months, compute the average month-end balance across all customers and provide the difference between these two averages
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_transactions_2020_cohort AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_date,
    LOWER(txn_type) AS txn_type,
    txn_amount,
    substr(txn_date,1,7) AS txn_ym
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE txn_date >= '2020-01-01' AND txn_date <= '2020-12-31'
),
customers_2020_active_list AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id
  FROM customer_transactions_2020_cohort
),
customer_monthly_balances_raw AS (
  SELECT
    ct.customer_id,
    ct.txn_ym,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ct.txn_type = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS sum_deposits,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ct.txn_type = 'deposit' THEN 0 ELSE ct.txn_amount END) AS sum_withdrawals,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ct.txn_type = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount ELSE -ct.txn_amount END) AS month_net_raw
  FROM customer_transactions_2020_cohort ct
  GROUP BY ct.customer_id, ct.txn_ym
),
months_2020 AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT txn_ym
  FROM customer_transactions_2020_cohort
),
month_stats AS (
  SELECT
    m.txn_ym,
    SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(mb.month_net_raw,0) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS positive_count,
    AVG(COALESCE(mb.month_net_raw,0)) AS avg_balance
  FROM customers_2020_active_list c
  CROSS JOIN months_2020 m
  LEFT JOIN customer_monthly_balances_raw mb
    ON mb.customer_id = c.customer_id AND mb.txn_ym = m.txn_ym
  GROUP BY m.txn_ym
),
highest_month AS (
  SELECT txn_ym, positive_count, avg_balance
  FROM (
    SELECT txn_ym, positive_count, avg_balance,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY positive_count DESC, txn_ym ASC) AS rn
    FROM month_stats
  ) t
  WHERE rn = 1
),
lowest_month AS (
  SELECT txn_ym, positive_count, avg_balance
  FROM (
    SELECT txn_ym, positive_count, avg_balance,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY positive_count ASC, txn_ym ASC) AS rn
    FROM month_stats
  ) t
  WHERE rn = 1
)
SELECT
  h.txn_ym AS month_label_for_highest_positive_count,
  h.positive_count AS positive_customer_count_for_highest_month,
  h.avg_balance AS average_month_end_balance_for_highest_month,
  l.txn_ym AS month_label_for_lowest_positive_count,
  l.positive_count AS positive_customer_count_for_lowest_month,
  l.avg_balance AS average_month_end_balance_for_lowest_month,
  (h.avg_balance - l.avg_balance) AS difference_between_averages
FROM highest_month h CROSS JOIN lowest_month l

rows.question: For each customer, group all deposits and withdrawals by the first day of each month to obtain a monthly net amount, then calculate each month’s closing balance by cumulatively summing these monthly nets. Next, determine the most recent month’s growth rate by comparing its closing balance to the prior month’s balance, treating deposits as positive and withdrawals as negative, and if the previous month’s balance is zero, the growth rate should be the current month’s balance multiplied by 100. Finally, compute the percentage of customers whose most recent month shows a growth rate of more than 5%.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_transactions_canonical AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    -- normalized month start as YYYY-MM-01
    substr(txn_date, 1, 7) || '-01' AS txn_date_month_start,
    CAST(substr(txn_date, 1, 4) AS INTEGER) AS txn_year,
    CAST(substr(txn_date, 6, 2) AS INTEGER) AS txn_month,
    txn_type,
    CASE
      WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
      WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'withdrawal' THEN -txn_amount
      WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'withdraw' THEN -txn_amount
      ELSE txn_amount
    END AS txn_amount_signed
  FROM customer_transactions
),
customer_monthly_net AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_date_month_start AS month_start,
    (txn_year * 100 + txn_month) AS month_order,
    SUM(txn_amount_signed) AS monthly_net
  FROM customer_transactions_canonical
  GROUP BY customer_id, txn_date_month_start, txn_year, txn_month
)
SELECT
  100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN growth_rate > 0.05 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) / COUNT(*) AS percentage_customers_growth_over_5_percent
FROM (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    CASE
      WHEN COALESCE(prior_closing_balance, 0) = 0
        THEN COALESCE(latest_closing_balance, 0) * 100.0
      ELSE
        (COALESCE(latest_closing_balance, 0) - prior_closing_balance) / prior_closing_balance
    END AS growth_rate
  FROM (
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      MAX(CASE WHEN month_rank = 1 THEN closing_balance END) AS latest_closing_balance,
      MAX(CASE WHEN month_rank = 2 THEN closing_balance END) AS prior_closing_balance
    FROM (
      SELECT
        customer_id,
        month_start,
        month_order,
        monthly_net,
        SUM(monthly_net) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_order ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS closing_balance,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_order DESC) AS month_rank
      FROM customer_monthly_net
    ) t
    WHERE month_rank <= 2
    GROUP BY customer_id
  ) per_customer
) final

rows.question: For each month, calculate the total balance from all users for the previous month (measured as of the 1st of each month), replacing any negative balances with zero. Ensure that data from the first month is used only as a baseline for calculating previous total balance, and exclude it from the final output. Sort the results in ascending order by month.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_transactions_raw AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    -- normalize txn_date to YYYY-MM-DD
    date(
      CASE
        WHEN length(txn_date) = 10 AND instr(txn_date, '-') = 5 THEN txn_date
        WHEN length(txn_date) = 10 AND instr(txn_date, '/') = 5 THEN substr(txn_date, 7, 4) || '-' || substr(txn_date, 4, 2) || '-' || substr(txn_date, 1, 2)
        ELSE txn_date
      END
    ) AS txn_date,
    CAST(txn_amount AS NUMERIC) AS txn_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
),
-- calendar of months present in the data
transaction_month_calendar AS (
  SELECT
    strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date) AS month,
    date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', txn_date)) AS month_first_day,
    date(date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', txn_date)), '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_last_day,
    CAST(strftime('%Y%m', txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS month_order
  FROM customer_transactions_raw
  GROUP BY month, month_first_day, month_last_day, month_order
),
-- for each customer compute cumulative balance up to each date present (use distinct dates to reduce rows)
customer_cumulative_by_date AS (
  SELECT
    ct.customer_id,
    d.txn_date AS as_of_date,
    (SELECT SUM(ct2.txn_amount)
     FROM customer_transactions_raw ct2
     WHERE ct2.customer_id = ct.customer_id
       AND date(ct2.txn_date) <= date(d.txn_date)
    ) AS cumulative_balance
  FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions_raw
  ) ct
  CROSS JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT txn_date FROM customer_transactions_raw
  ) d
),
-- For each month M (after the earliest), we need cumulative balances as of last day of previous month.
-- So join months to previous month's last day and sum the per-customer cumulative balances as of that date.
months_with_prev AS (
  SELECT
    m.month,
    m.month_order,
    prev.month_last_day AS prev_month_last_day
  FROM transaction_month_calendar m
  JOIN transaction_month_calendar prev
    ON m.month_order = prev.month_order + 1
)
SELECT
  m.month,
  -- sum the latest cumulative balance per customer as of prev_month_last_day; replace negative totals with 0
  CASE WHEN SUM(COALESCE(cb.cumulative_balance, 0.0)) < 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE SUM(COALESCE(cb.cumulative_balance, 0.0)) END AS prev_month_total_balance
FROM months_with_prev m
LEFT JOIN customer_cumulative_by_date cb
  ON date(cb.as_of_date) = date(m.prev_month_last_day)
GROUP BY m.month, m.month_order
ORDER BY m.month ASC

rows.question: For a bank database with customer transactions, calculate each customer's daily running balance (where deposits add to the balance and other transaction types subtract). For each customer and each day, compute the 30-day rolling average balance (only after having 30 days of data, and treating negative averages as zero). Then group these daily averages by month and find each customer's maximum 30-day average balance within each month. Sum these maximum values across all customers for each month. Consider the first month of each customer's transaction history as the baseline period and exclude it from the final results, presenting monthly totals of these summed maximum 30-day average balances.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_daily_net_txn AS (
  SELECT
    ct.customer_id,
    ct.txn_date,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ct.txn_type = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount ELSE -ct.txn_amount END) AS net_amount
  FROM customer_transactions ct
  GROUP BY ct.customer_id, ct.txn_date
),
customer_first_transaction_month AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    substr(min(txn_date),1,7) AS first_txn_month
  FROM customer_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
-- precompute for each customer-date the 30-day window sum and the count of distinct days up to that date
customer_30d_window AS (
  SELECT
    d1.customer_id,
    d1.txn_date AS date,
    SUM(d2.net_amount) AS window_sum,
    COUNT(DISTINCT d3.txn_date) AS days_up_to_date
  FROM customer_daily_net_txn d1
  JOIN customer_daily_net_txn d2
    ON d1.customer_id = d2.customer_id
   AND DATE(d2.txn_date) BETWEEN DATE(d1.txn_date, '-29 days') AND DATE(d1.txn_date)
  JOIN customer_daily_net_txn d3
    ON d1.customer_id = d3.customer_id
   AND DATE(d3.txn_date) <= DATE(d1.txn_date)
  GROUP BY d1.customer_id, d1.txn_date
),
customer_30d_rolling_avg_balance AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date,
    CASE WHEN days_up_to_date >= 30 THEN MAX(0.0, window_sum / 30.0) ELSE NULL END AS rolling_30d_avg_nonneg
  FROM customer_30d_window
)
SELECT
  month,
  SUM(monthly_max) AS total_summed_max_30d_avg_balance
FROM (
  SELECT
    r.customer_id,
    substr(r.date,1,7) AS month,
    MAX(r.rolling_30d_avg_nonneg) AS monthly_max
  FROM customer_30d_rolling_avg_balance r
  JOIN customer_first_transaction_month f
    ON r.customer_id = f.customer_id
  WHERE r.rolling_30d_avg_nonneg IS NOT NULL
    AND substr(r.date,1,7) <> f.first_txn_month
  GROUP BY r.customer_id, substr(r.date,1,7)
) per_cust_month
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month ASC

rows.question: For each customer, calculate their daily balances for every day between their earliest and latest transaction dates, including days without transactions by carrying forward the previous day's balance. Treat any negative daily balances as zero. Then, for each month, determine the highest daily balance each customer had during that month. Finally, for each month, sum these maximum daily balances across all customers to obtain a monthly total.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH
-- normalize and aggregate transactions per customer per ISO date (assume most inputs already YYYY-MM-DD)
customer_transaction_daily_raw AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    -- keep txn_date as-is; SQLite date() will parse ISO YYYY-MM-DD properly
    date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
    SUM(txn_amount) AS daily_txn_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id, date(txn_date)
),
-- per-customer date bounds based on normalized dates
customer_transaction_date_bounds AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    MIN(txn_date) AS first_txn_date,
    MAX(txn_date) AS last_txn_date
  FROM customer_transaction_daily_raw
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
-- generate calendar of dates per customer between first and last txn dates (inclusive)
customer_calendar AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    first_txn_date AS calendar_date,
    first_txn_date,
    last_txn_date
  FROM customer_transaction_date_bounds
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(calendar_date, '+1 day') AS calendar_date,
    first_txn_date,
    last_txn_date
  FROM customer_calendar
  WHERE date(calendar_date, '+1 day') <= last_txn_date
),
-- attach daily txn amounts (0 if none) to each date
customer_daily_running_balance_prep AS (
  SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    c.calendar_date,
    COALESCE(r.daily_txn_amount, 0) AS daily_txn_amount
  FROM customer_calendar c
  LEFT JOIN customer_transaction_daily_raw r
    ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id
    AND r.txn_date = c.calendar_date
),
-- compute running balances per customer per day
customer_daily_running_balance AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    calendar_date,
    SUM(daily_txn_amount) OVER (
      PARTITION BY customer_id
      ORDER BY calendar_date
      ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS running_balance_raw
  FROM customer_daily_running_balance_prep
),
-- per customer per month max daily balance (clamp negatives to zero before taking max)
customer_month_max AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    strftime('%Y-%m', calendar_date) AS month,
    MAX(CASE WHEN running_balance_raw < 0 THEN 0 ELSE running_balance_raw END) AS customer_month_max
  FROM customer_daily_running_balance
  GROUP BY customer_id, month
)
-- final: sum the per-customer monthly maxima across customers
SELECT
  month,
  SUM(customer_month_max) AS monthly_total_max_balances
FROM customer_month_max
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month

rows.question: Can you provide a breakdown of how many times each product was viewed, how many times they were added to the shopping cart, and how many times they were left in the cart without being purchased? Also, give me the count of actual purchases for each product. Ensure that products with a page id in (1, 2, 12, 13) are filtered out.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH shopping_cart_page_product_lookup AS (
  SELECT page_id, page_name, product_id, product_category
  FROM shopping_cart_page_hierarchy
  WHERE product_id IS NOT NULL
    AND page_id NOT IN (1,2,12,13)
),
shopping_cart_events_enriched AS (
  SELECT
    e.visit_id,
    e.cookie_id,
    e.event_time,
    e.page_id,
    p.product_id,
    p.page_name AS product_name,
    LOWER(COALESCE(sei.event_name, '')) AS event_name_lc
  FROM shopping_cart_events e
  JOIN shopping_cart_page_product_lookup p
    ON e.page_id = p.page_id
  LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_event_identifier sei
    ON e.event_type = sei.event_type
  WHERE e.page_id NOT IN (1,2,12,13)
),
-- For each product & visit determine whether there was an add_to_cart and/or purchase
per_visit_flags AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    visit_id,
    MAX(CASE WHEN event_name_lc = 'add to cart' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS had_add,
    MAX(CASE WHEN event_name_lc = 'purchase' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS had_purchase
  FROM shopping_cart_events_enriched
  WHERE visit_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY product_id, visit_id
)
SELECT
  p.product_id,
  p.page_name AS product_name,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name_lc = 'page view' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) AS view_count,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name_lc = 'add to cart' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) AS add_to_cart_count,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name_lc = 'purchase' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) AS purchase_count,
  -- abandoned_count: number of distinct visits that had an add_to_cart for the product but no purchase
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN pv.had_add = 1 AND pv.had_purchase = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) AS abandoned_count
FROM shopping_cart_page_product_lookup p
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_events_enriched e
  ON e.product_id = p.product_id
LEFT JOIN per_visit_flags pv
  ON pv.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.page_name
ORDER BY view_count DESC

rows.question: Please analyze our interest data from September 2018 to August 2019. For each month, calculate the average composition for each interest by dividing the composition by the index value. Identify the interest with the highest average composition value each month and report its average composition as the max index composition for that month. Compute the three-month rolling average of these monthly max index compositions. Ensure the output includes the date, the interest name, the max index composition for that month, the rolling average, and the names and max index compositions of the top interests from one month ago and two months ago.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH interest_metrics_filtered_by_valid_index AS (
  SELECT
    interest_id,
    _year,
    _month,
    month_year,
    composition,
    index_value
  FROM interest_metrics
  WHERE index_value IS NOT NULL
    AND index_value <> 0
    AND _year IS NOT NULL
    AND _month IS NOT NULL
    AND month_year IS NOT NULL
    -- restrict to requested months 2018-09 through 2019-08
    AND (
      (_year = 2018 AND _month IN (9,10,11,12))
      OR (_year = 2019 AND _month IN (1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8))
    )
),
interest_monthly_index_composition AS (
  -- compute per-month-per-interest composition / index_value (use averages across any duplicate rows)
  SELECT
    _year,
    _month,
    month_year AS month_key,
    interest_id,
    AVG(composition) AS avg_composition,
    AVG(index_value) AS avg_index_value,
    (AVG(composition) * 1.0) / AVG(index_value) AS composition_div_index
  FROM interest_metrics_filtered_by_valid_index
  GROUP BY _year, _month, month_year, interest_id
),
-- for each month pick the interest(s) with the highest composition_div_index
monthly_max_candidates AS (
  SELECT
    imi._year,
    imi._month,
    imi.month_key,
    imi.interest_id,
    imi.composition_div_index
  FROM interest_monthly_index_composition imi
  JOIN (
    SELECT month_key, MAX(composition_div_index) AS max_cdi
    FROM interest_monthly_index_composition
    GROUP BY month_key
  ) m ON imi.month_key = m.month_key AND imi.composition_div_index = m.max_cdi
),
-- break ties by smallest interest_id deterministically
monthly_max_interest AS (
  SELECT
    mc._year,
    mc._month,
    mc.month_key,
    mc.interest_id,
    mc.composition_div_index AS max_index_composition
  FROM monthly_max_candidates mc
  JOIN (
    SELECT month_key, MIN(interest_id) AS interest_id
    FROM monthly_max_candidates
    GROUP BY month_key
  ) tie ON mc.month_key = tie.month_key AND mc.interest_id = tie.interest_id
),
-- attach interest_name (or placeholder) and compute lagged values and 3-month rolling avg
monthly_with_history AS (
  SELECT
    mm.month_key,
    mm._year,
    mm._month,
    mm.interest_id,
    COALESCE(imap.interest_name, 'interest_id:' || mm.interest_id) AS interest_name,
    mm.max_index_composition,
    LAG(mm._year || '-' || printf('%02d', mm._month), 1) OVER (ORDER BY mm._year, mm._month) AS prev1_month_key,
    LAG(mm.interest_id, 1) OVER (ORDER BY mm._year, mm._month) AS prev1_interest_id,
    LAG(mm.max_index_composition, 1) OVER (ORDER BY mm._year, mm._month) AS prev1_max_index_composition,
    LAG(mm._year || '-' || printf('%02d', mm._month), 2) OVER (ORDER BY mm._year, mm._month) AS prev2_month_key,
    LAG(mm.interest_id, 2) OVER (ORDER BY mm._year, mm._month) AS prev2_interest_id,
    LAG(mm.max_index_composition, 2) OVER (ORDER BY mm._year, mm._month) AS prev2_max_index_composition,
    ( (mm.max_index_composition
       + LAG(mm.max_index_composition,1) OVER (ORDER BY mm._year, mm._month)
       + LAG(mm.max_index_composition,2) OVER (ORDER BY mm._year, mm._month)
      ) / 3.0
    ) AS rolling_avg_3mo_candidate
  FROM monthly_max_interest mm
  LEFT JOIN interest_map imap ON mm.interest_id = imap.id
)
SELECT
  -- output month as YYYY-MM-01 date-like string per requirement (use YYYY-MM-01)
  (_year || '-' || printf('%02d', _month) || '-01') AS month,
  interest_name,
  max_index_composition,
  CASE
    WHEN max_index_composition IS NOT NULL
     AND prev1_max_index_composition IS NOT NULL
     AND prev2_max_index_composition IS NOT NULL
    THEN rolling_avg_3mo_candidate
    ELSE NULL
  END AS rolling_avg_3mo,
  -- for prev names, map ids to names (use placeholder if missing)
  (SELECT COALESCE(im.interest_name, 'interest_id:' || mwh.prev1_interest_id)
   FROM (SELECT 1) AS _dummy
   LEFT JOIN interest_map im ON im.id = mwh.prev1_interest_id
  ) AS prev1_interest_name,
  prev1_max_index_composition,
  (SELECT COALESCE(im2.interest_name, 'interest_id:' || mwh.prev2_interest_id)
   FROM (SELECT 1) AS _dummy2
   LEFT JOIN interest_map im2 ON im2.id = mwh.prev2_interest_id
  ) AS prev2_interest_name,
  prev2_max_index_composition
FROM monthly_with_history mwh
ORDER BY _year, _month

rows.question: Identify the top 10 and bottom 10 interest categories based on their highest composition values across all months. For each category, display the time(MM-YYYY), interest name, and the composition value
rows.pred_sql:
WITH interest_metrics_rows AS (
  SELECT
    interest_id,
    _year,
    _month,
    month_year,
    composition
  FROM interest_metrics
  WHERE interest_id IS NOT NULL
),
max_comp_by_interest AS (
  SELECT
    interest_id,
    MAX(composition) AS max_composition
  FROM interest_metrics_rows
  GROUP BY interest_id
),
-- choose the most recent month when the max composition occurred
max_comp_latest_month AS (
  SELECT
    m.interest_id,
    m.max_composition,
    imr.month_year,
    imr._year,
    imr._month
  FROM max_comp_by_interest m
  JOIN interest_metrics_rows imr
    ON imr.interest_id = m.interest_id
   AND imr.composition = m.max_composition
  -- keep only the most recent (_year, _month) for ties
  WHERE (_year, _month) = (
    SELECT imr2._year, imr2._month
    FROM interest_metrics_rows imr2
    WHERE imr2.interest_id = imr.interest_id
      AND imr2.composition = imr.composition
    ORDER BY imr2._year DESC, imr2._month DESC
    LIMIT 1
  )
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT
    mc.interest_id,
    mc.month_year,
    mc.max_composition AS composition,
    im.interest_name,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY mc.max_composition DESC, mc.interest_id) AS rn_desc,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY mc.max_composition ASC, mc.interest_id) AS rn_asc
  FROM max_comp_latest_month mc
  JOIN interest_map im ON im.id = mc.interest_id
),
selected AS (
  SELECT month_year, interest_name, composition, rn_desc, rn_asc, 1 AS list_order
  FROM ranked
  WHERE rn_desc <= 10
  UNION ALL
  SELECT month_year, interest_name, composition, rn_desc, rn_asc, 2 AS list_order
  FROM ranked
  WHERE rn_asc <= 10
)
SELECT month_year, interest_name, composition
FROM selected
ORDER BY
  list_order, 
  CASE WHEN list_order = 1 THEN rn_desc ELSE rn_asc END

rows.question: Analyze the annual average purchase price per Bitcoin by region, computed as the total dollar amount spent divided by the total quantity purchased each year, excluding the first year's data for each region. Then, for each year, rank the regions based on these average purchase prices, and calculate the annual percentage change in cost for each region compared to the previous year.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH bitcoin_transaction_buy_events AS (
  SELECT
    btc.txn_id,
    btc.member_id,
    btc.ticker,
    -- normalize txn_date assumed formats DD-MM-YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD; else keep as-is
    CASE
      WHEN instr(btc.txn_date,'-') = 3 AND length(btc.txn_date) = 10
        THEN substr(btc.txn_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(btc.txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(btc.txn_date,1,2)
      WHEN instr(btc.txn_date,'-') = 5 AND length(btc.txn_date) = 10
        THEN btc.txn_date
      ELSE btc.txn_date
    END AS txn_date_iso,
    -- extract year (first 4 chars of normalized string when possible)
    CASE
      WHEN length(
        CASE
          WHEN instr(btc.txn_date,'-') = 3 AND length(btc.txn_date) = 10 THEN substr(btc.txn_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(btc.txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(btc.txn_date,1,2)
          WHEN instr(btc.txn_date,'-') = 5 AND length(btc.txn_date) = 10 THEN btc.txn_date
          ELSE btc.txn_date
        END
      ) >= 4 THEN substr(
        CASE
          WHEN instr(btc.txn_date,'-') = 3 AND length(btc.txn_date) = 10 THEN substr(btc.txn_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(btc.txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(btc.txn_date,1,2)
          WHEN instr(btc.txn_date,'-') = 5 AND length(btc.txn_date) = 10 THEN btc.txn_date
          ELSE btc.txn_date
        END, 1, 4)
      ELSE NULL
    END AS txn_year,
    btc.txn_type,
    btc.quantity,
    btc.percentage_fee,
    btc.txn_time,
    bm.region AS member_region
  FROM bitcoin_transactions btc
  LEFT JOIN bitcoin_members bm ON btc.member_id = bm.member_id
  WHERE btc.txn_type = 'BUY'
),
bitcoin_market_price_by_date AS (
  SELECT
    ticker,
    market_date,
    -- normalize market_date formats DD-MM-YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD when possible
    CASE
      WHEN instr(market_date,'-') = 3 AND length(market_date) = 10
        THEN substr(market_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(market_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(market_date,1,2)
      WHEN instr(market_date,'-') = 5 AND length(market_date) = 10
        THEN market_date
      ELSE NULL
    END AS market_date_iso,
    -- parse numeric price (remove commas and percent signs; ensure no letters)
    CASE
      WHEN price IS NULL OR trim(price) = '' THEN NULL
      ELSE
        CASE
          WHEN replace(replace(price,',',''),'%','') GLOB '*[0-9]*' AND replace(replace(price,',',''),'%','') NOT GLOB '*[A-Za-z]*'
            THEN CAST(replace(replace(price,',',''),'%','') AS REAL)
          ELSE NULL
        END
    END AS price_usd,
    rowid AS price_rowid
  FROM bitcoin_prices
),
-- join transactions to market prices on ticker and date; aggregate per region & year
region_year AS (
  SELECT
    t.member_region AS region,
    t.txn_year AS calendar_year,
    SUM(t.quantity * p.price_usd) AS total_amount_spent_usd,
    SUM(t.quantity) AS total_quantity,
    CASE WHEN SUM(t.quantity) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE SUM(t.quantity * p.price_usd) / SUM(t.quantity) END AS avg_price_per_btc
  FROM bitcoin_transaction_buy_events t
  JOIN bitcoin_market_price_by_date p
    ON t.ticker = p.ticker
    AND date(t.txn_date_iso) = date(p.market_date_iso)
    AND p.price_usd IS NOT NULL
  WHERE t.txn_year IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY t.member_region, t.txn_year
  HAVING SUM(t.quantity) > 0
),
-- determine first year of activity per region to exclude it later
first_year_per_region AS (
  SELECT region, MIN(calendar_year) AS first_txn_year_for_region
  FROM region_year
  GROUP BY region
)
SELECT
  ry.calendar_year AS year,
  ry.region,
  ry.total_amount_spent_usd,
  ry.total_quantity,
  ry.avg_price_per_btc,
  -- rank regions within year by avg price desc
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY ry.calendar_year ORDER BY ry.avg_price_per_btc DESC) AS region_rank_in_year,
  -- percent change vs previous year for same region
  CASE
    WHEN prev.avg_price_per_btc IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN prev.avg_price_per_btc = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE ((ry.avg_price_per_btc - prev.avg_price_per_btc) / prev.avg_price_per_btc) * 100.0
  END AS pct_change_vs_prev_year
FROM region_year ry
LEFT JOIN region_year prev
  ON prev.region = ry.region
  AND CAST(prev.calendar_year AS INTEGER) = CAST(ry.calendar_year AS INTEGER) - 1
LEFT JOIN first_year_per_region fy
  ON fy.region = ry.region
WHERE ry.calendar_year IS NOT NULL
  AND ry.avg_price_per_btc IS NOT NULL
  AND ry.total_quantity > 0
  -- exclude the first year of data for the region
  AND CAST(ry.calendar_year AS INTEGER) <> CAST(fy.first_txn_year_for_region AS INTEGER)
ORDER BY CAST(ry.calendar_year AS INTEGER) ASC,
         region_rank_in_year ASC

rows.question: Using the "bitcoin_prices" table, please calculate the daily percentage change in trading volume for each ticker from August 1 to August 10, 2021, ensuring that any volume ending in "K" or "M" is accurately converted to thousands or millions, any "-" volume is treated as zero, only non-zero volumes are used to determine the previous day's volume, and the results are ordered by ticker and date.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH bitcoin_prices_raw AS (
  SELECT
    ticker,
    market_date,
    volume
  FROM bitcoin_prices
  WHERE ticker IS NOT NULL
    AND market_date >= '01-08-2021'
    AND market_date <= '10-08-2021'
),
bitcoin_prices_volume_normalized AS (
  SELECT
    ticker,
    market_date,
    -- normalize volume: '-' => 0, 'K' => *1_000, 'M' => *1_000_000, else numeric (remove commas/spaces)
    CASE
      WHEN volume = '-' THEN 0.0
      WHEN volume LIKE '%K' THEN
        CAST(replace(replace(substr(volume, 1, length(volume)-1), ',', ''), ' ', '') AS REAL) * 1000.0
      WHEN volume LIKE '%M' THEN
        CAST(replace(replace(substr(volume, 1, length(volume)-1), ',', ''), ' ', '') AS REAL) * 1000000.0
      ELSE
        CAST(replace(replace(volume, ',', ''), ' ', '') AS REAL)
    END AS volume_normalized,
    -- also compute an ISO date to make calendar-day arithmetic simple
    date(substr(market_date, 7, 4) || '-' || substr(market_date, 4, 2) || '-' || substr(market_date, 1, 2)) AS iso_date
  FROM bitcoin_prices_raw
),
prev_day_lookup AS (
  -- for each row, find the row for same ticker and iso_date - 1
  SELECT
    cur.ticker,
    cur.market_date,
    cur.iso_date,
    cur.volume_normalized,
    prev.volume_normalized AS prev_day_volume_normalized
  FROM bitcoin_prices_volume_normalized cur
  LEFT JOIN bitcoin_prices_volume_normalized prev
    ON cur.ticker = prev.ticker
   AND prev.iso_date = date(cur.iso_date, '-1 day')
)
SELECT
  ticker,
  market_date,
  volume_normalized,
  -- per requirement: if prior-day missing or zero, return NULL for prev_day_volume_normalized
  CASE
    WHEN prev_day_volume_normalized IS NULL OR prev_day_volume_normalized = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE prev_day_volume_normalized
  END AS prev_day_volume_normalized,
  CASE
    WHEN prev_day_volume_normalized IS NULL OR prev_day_volume_normalized = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (volume_normalized - prev_day_volume_normalized) / prev_day_volume_normalized * 100.0
  END AS pct_change_volume
FROM prev_day_lookup
ORDER BY ticker ASC, market_date ASC

rows.question: For veg whsle data, can you generate a summary of our items' loss rates? Include the average loss rate, and also break down the count of items that are below, above, and within one standard deviation from this average.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH veg_loss_rate_rows AS (
  SELECT
    "item_code",
    "item_name",
    "loss_rate_%" AS loss_rate
  FROM "veg_loss_rate_df"
  WHERE "loss_rate_%" IS NOT NULL
),
stats AS (
  SELECT
    AVG(loss_rate) AS avg_loss,
    CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN NULL
         ELSE sqrt(AVG(loss_rate * loss_rate) - AVG(loss_rate) * AVG(loss_rate))
    END AS stddev_loss,
    COUNT(*) AS total_items
  FROM veg_loss_rate_rows
)
SELECT
  s.avg_loss AS average_loss_rate_percent,
  s.stddev_loss AS stddev_loss_rate_percent,
  SUM(CASE WHEN v.loss_rate < s.avg_loss THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_below_mean,
  SUM(CASE WHEN s.stddev_loss IS NOT NULL
           AND v.loss_rate BETWEEN s.avg_loss - s.stddev_loss AND s.avg_loss + s.stddev_loss
           THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_within_one_stddev,
  SUM(CASE WHEN v.loss_rate > s.avg_loss THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_above_mean,
  s.total_items AS total_items_considered
FROM veg_loss_rate_rows v
CROSS JOIN stats s

rows.question: For veg whsle data, can you analyze our financial performance over the years 2020 to 2023? I need insights into the average wholesale price, maximum wholesale price, minimum wholesale price, wholesale price difference, total wholesale price, total selling price, average loss rate, total loss, and profit for each category within each year. Round all calculated values to two decimal places.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH veg_item_category_map AS (
  SELECT item_code, item_name, category_code, category_name
  FROM veg_cat
),
veg_wholesale_by_item_year AS (
  SELECT
    item_code,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', whsle_date) AS INTEGER) AS whsle_year,
    "whsle_px_rmb-kg" AS whsle_px_rmb_kg
  FROM veg_whsle_df
  WHERE whsle_date IS NOT NULL
    AND "whsle_px_rmb-kg" IS NOT NULL
),
veg_txn_with_loss_and_year AS (
  SELECT
    vtd.item_code,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS txn_year,
    vtd."qty_sold(kg)" AS qty_sold_kg,
    vtd."unit_selling_px_rmb/kg" AS unit_selling_px_rmb_kg,
    COALESCE(vlr."loss_rate_%", 0.0) AS loss_rate_percent,
    COALESCE(vlr."loss_rate_%", 0.0) / 100.0 AS loss_fraction
  FROM veg_txn_df vtd
  LEFT JOIN veg_loss_rate_df vlr ON vtd.item_code = vlr.item_code
  WHERE vtd.txn_date IS NOT NULL
    AND vtd."qty_sold(kg)" IS NOT NULL
    AND vtd."unit_selling_px_rmb/kg" IS NOT NULL
),
-- aggregate wholesale metrics per category-year
wholesale_cat_year AS (
  SELECT
    vwm.category_name,
    vwy.whsle_year AS year,
    AVG(vwy.whsle_px_rmb_kg) AS avg_whsle_price,
    MAX(vwy.whsle_px_rmb_kg) AS max_whsle_price,
    MIN(vwy.whsle_px_rmb_kg) AS min_whsle_price,
    SUM(vwy.whsle_px_rmb_kg) AS total_whsle_price
  FROM veg_wholesale_by_item_year vwy
  JOIN veg_item_category_map vwm ON vwy.item_code = vwm.item_code
  WHERE vwy.whsle_year IN (2020,2021,2022,2023) AND vwm.category_name IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY vwy.whsle_year, vwm.category_name
),
-- aggregate transaction metrics per category-year
txn_cat_year AS (
  SELECT
    vwm.category_name,
    vtx.txn_year AS year,
    SUM(vtx.qty_sold_kg * vtx.unit_selling_px_rmb_kg) AS total_selling_price,
    AVG(vtx.loss_rate_percent) AS avg_loss_rate_percent,
    SUM(vtx.qty_sold_kg * vtx.unit_selling_px_rmb_kg * vtx.loss_fraction) AS total_loss_value,
    SUM(vtx.qty_sold_kg) AS total_qty_sold_kg
  FROM veg_txn_with_loss_and_year vtx
  JOIN veg_item_category_map vwm ON vtx.item_code = vwm.item_code
  WHERE vtx.txn_year IN (2020,2021,2022,2023) AND vwm.category_name IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY vtx.txn_year, vwm.category_name
),
-- compute wholesale cost for sold quantities by matching wholesale price by item-year where available
whsle_cost_cat_year AS (
  SELECT
    vwm.category_name,
    vtx.txn_year AS year,
    SUM(vtx.qty_sold_kg * COALESCE(vwy.whsle_px_rmb_kg, 0.0)) AS total_whsle_cost
  FROM veg_txn_with_loss_and_year vtx
  JOIN veg_item_category_map vwm ON vtx.item_code = vwm.item_code
  LEFT JOIN veg_wholesale_by_item_year vwy
    ON vwy.item_code = vtx.item_code
    AND vwy.whsle_year = vtx.txn_year
  WHERE vtx.txn_year IN (2020,2021,2022,2023) AND vwm.category_name IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY vtx.txn_year, vwm.category_name
),
-- union all category-year keys from the three sources to emulate full outer join
all_category_years AS (
  SELECT year, category_name FROM wholesale_cat_year
  UNION
  SELECT year, category_name FROM txn_cat_year
  UNION
  SELECT year, category_name FROM whsle_cost_cat_year
)
SELECT
  a.year AS year,
  a.category_name AS category_name,
  ROUND(COALESCE(w.avg_whsle_price, 0.0), 2) AS avg_whsle_price,
  ROUND(COALESCE(w.max_whsle_price, 0.0), 2) AS max_whsle_price,
  ROUND(COALESCE(w.min_whsle_price, 0.0), 2) AS min_whsle_price,
  ROUND(COALESCE(w.max_whsle_price, 0.0) - COALESCE(w.min_whsle_price, 0.0), 2) AS whsle_price_diff,
  ROUND(COALESCE(w.total_whsle_price, 0.0), 2) AS total_whsle_price,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t.total_selling_price, 0.0), 2) AS total_selling_price,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t.avg_loss_rate_percent, 0.0), 2) AS avg_loss_rate_percent,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t.total_loss_value, 0.0), 2) AS total_loss_value,
  ROUND(
    COALESCE(t.total_selling_price, 0.0)
    - COALESCE(c.total_whsle_cost, 0.0)
    - COALESCE(t.total_loss_value, 0.0)
  , 2) AS profit
FROM all_category_years a
LEFT JOIN wholesale_cat_year w ON a.year = w.year AND a.category_name = w.category_name
LEFT JOIN txn_cat_year t ON a.year = t.year AND a.category_name = t.category_name
LEFT JOIN whsle_cost_cat_year c ON a.year = c.year AND a.category_name = c.category_name
WHERE a.year IN (2020,2021,2022,2023)
ORDER BY a.year ASC, a.category_name ASC

rows.question: For weekly-sales data, I need an analysis of our sales performance around mid-June for the years 2018, 2019, and 2020. Specifically, calculate the percentage change in sales between the four weeks leading up to June 15 and the four weeks following June 15 for each year.

WITH weekly_sales_aggregated_by_week_start AS (
  SELECT
    week_date,
    calendar_year,
    SUM(sales) AS total_sales
  FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
  GROUP BY calendar_year, week_date
),
target_weeks AS (
  -- determine the week_start (week_date) that contains June 15 for each year 2018-2020
  SELECT
    y.calendar_year,
    w.week_date AS week_start_date
  FROM (SELECT 2018 AS calendar_year UNION ALL SELECT 2019 UNION ALL SELECT 2020) AS y
  LEFT JOIN weekly_sales_aggregated_by_week_start AS w
    ON w.calendar_year = y.calendar_year
    -- week starting on w.week_date (inclusive) and ending the day before w.week_date + 7 days
    AND date(w.week_date) <= date(y.calendar_year || '-06-15')
    AND date(w.week_date, '+7 days') > date(y.calendar_year || '-06-15')
)
SELECT
  t.calendar_year,
  -- pre period = four weeks leading up to (but not including) the week that contains June 15
  MIN(pre.week_date) AS pre_period_start_date,
  MAX(pre.week_date) AS pre_period_end_date,
  COALESCE(SUM(pre.total_sales), 0) AS pre_period_sales,
  -- post period = the week containing June 15 and the following three weeks
  MIN(post.week_date) AS post_period_start_date,
  MAX(post.week_date) AS post_period_end_date,
  COALESCE(SUM(post.total_sales), 0) AS post_period_sales,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(SUM(pre.total_sales), 0) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE ((COALESCE(SUM(post.total_sales), 0) - COALESCE(SUM(pre.total_sales), 0))
          / CAST(COALESCE(SUM(pre.total_sales), 0) AS REAL)) * 100
  END AS pct_change
FROM target_weeks AS t
LEFT JOIN weekly_sales_aggregated_by_week_start AS post
  ON post.calendar_year = t.calendar_year
  AND post.week_date IN (
    date(t.week_start_date),
    date(t.week_start_date, '+7 days'),
    date(t.week_start_date, '+14 days'),
    date(t.week_start_date, '+21 days')
  )
LEFT JOIN weekly_sales_aggregated_by_week_start AS pre
  ON pre.calendar_year = t.calendar_year
  AND pre.week_date IN (
    date(t.week_start_date, '-28 days'),
    date(t.week_start_date, '-21 days'),
    date(t.week_start_date, '-14 days'),
    date(t.week_start_date, '-7 days')
  )
GROUP BY t.calendar_year
ORDER BY t.calendar_year

rows.question: Analyze the average percentage change in sales between the 12 weeks before and after June 15, 2020, for each attribute type: region, platform, age band, demographic, and customer type. For each attribute type, calculate the average percentage change in sales across all its attribute values. Identify the attribute type with the highest negative impact on sales and provide its average percentage change in sales.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH weekly_sales_core AS (
  SELECT
    week_date,
    sales,
    region,
    platform,
    age_band,
    demographic,
    customer_type
  FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
),
-- identify the 12 weeks before cutoff (strictly before 2020-06-15) and 12 weeks after (strictly after)
selected_weeks AS (
  SELECT week_date, 'before' AS period
  FROM (
    SELECT week_date
    FROM weekly_sales_core
    WHERE date(week_date) < date('2020-06-15')
    GROUP BY week_date
    ORDER BY date(week_date) DESC
    LIMIT 12
  )
  UNION ALL
  SELECT week_date, 'after' AS period
  FROM (
    SELECT week_date
    FROM weekly_sales_core
    WHERE date(week_date) > date('2020-06-15')
    GROUP BY week_date
    ORDER BY date(week_date) ASC
    LIMIT 12
  )
),
-- attach period to rows and keep only rows in the selected weeks
sales_with_period AS (
  SELECT wsc.*, sw.period
  FROM weekly_sales_core wsc
  JOIN selected_weeks sw ON date(wsc.week_date) = date(sw.week_date)
),
-- for each attribute type and attribute value compute total sales in each window and pct_change
attribute_value_pct_change_between_windows AS (
  SELECT
    attribute_type,
    attribute_value,
    SUM(CASE WHEN period = 'before' THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS total_sales_before,
    SUM(CASE WHEN period = 'after' THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS total_sales_after,
    CASE
      WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN period = 'before' THEN sales ELSE 0 END) = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE (CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN period = 'after' THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS REAL)
            - CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN period = 'before' THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS REAL))
           / CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN period = 'before' THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS REAL)
    END AS pct_change
  FROM (
    SELECT 'region' AS attribute_type, region AS attribute_value, period, sales FROM sales_with_period
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'platform' AS attribute_type, platform AS attribute_value, period, sales FROM sales_with_period
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'age_band' AS attribute_type, age_band AS attribute_value, period, sales FROM sales_with_period
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'demographic' AS attribute_type, demographic AS attribute_value, period, sales FROM sales_with_period
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'customer_type' AS attribute_type, customer_type AS attribute_value, period, sales FROM sales_with_period
  ) t
  GROUP BY attribute_type, attribute_value
  HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN period = 'before' THEN sales ELSE 0 END) > 0
)
,
-- average pct_change across attribute values for each attribute type
attribute_type_averages AS (
  SELECT
    attribute_type,
    AVG(pct_change) AS average_pct_change_across_attribute_values
  FROM attribute_value_pct_change_between_windows
  WHERE pct_change IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY attribute_type
)
-- final: return each attribute_type with its average, and also the single attribute_type with the most negative average
SELECT
  ata.attribute_type,
  ata.average_pct_change_across_attribute_values,
  (SELECT attribute_type FROM attribute_type_averages ORDER BY average_pct_change_across_attribute_values ASC LIMIT 1) AS attribute_type_with_highest_negative_impact,
  (SELECT average_pct_change_across_attribute_values FROM attribute_type_averages ORDER BY average_pct_change_across_attribute_values ASC LIMIT 1) AS highest_negative_average_pct_change
FROM attribute_type_averages ata
ORDER BY ata.average_pct_change_across_attribute_values ASC

rows.question: Please help me identify the top 3 bowlers who, in the overs where the maximum runs were conceded in each match, gave up the highest number of runs in a single over across all matches. For each of these bowlers, provide the match in which they conceded these maximum runs. Only consider overs that had the most runs conceded within their respective matches, and among these, determine which bowlers conceded the most runs in a single over overall.

WITH ball_delivery_canonical AS (
  SELECT
    match_id,
    innings_no,
    over_id,
    ball_id,
    bowler,
    team_batting,
    team_bowling
  FROM ball_by_ball
),
delivery_run_components AS (
  SELECT
    d.match_id,
    d.innings_no,
    d.over_id,
    d.ball_id,
    COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) AS runs_scored,
    COALESCE(er.extra_runs, 0) AS extra_runs
  FROM ball_delivery_canonical d
  LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
    ON bs.match_id = d.match_id
    AND bs.innings_no = d.innings_no
    AND bs.over_id = d.over_id
    AND bs.ball_id = d.ball_id
  LEFT JOIN extra_runs er
    ON er.match_id = d.match_id
    AND er.innings_no = d.innings_no
    AND er.over_id = d.over_id
    AND er.ball_id = d.ball_id
),
-- compute runs conceded per over
over_runs AS (
  SELECT
    d.match_id,
    d.innings_no,
    d.over_id,
    SUM(d.runs_scored + d.extra_runs) AS runs_conceded_in_over
  FROM delivery_run_components d
  GROUP BY d.match_id, d.innings_no, d.over_id
),
-- compute delivery counts by bowler per over (to pick majority bowler(s))
bowler_delivery_counts AS (
  SELECT
    b.match_id,
    b.innings_no,
    b.over_id,
    b.bowler AS bowler_id,
    COUNT(*) AS deliveries_by_this_bowler
  FROM ball_delivery_canonical b
  GROUP BY b.match_id, b.innings_no, b.over_id, b.bowler
),
-- total deliveries per over
total_deliveries AS (
  SELECT
    match_id,
    innings_no,
    over_id,
    SUM(deliveries_by_this_bowler) AS total_deliveries_in_over
  FROM bowler_delivery_counts
  GROUP BY match_id, innings_no, over_id
),
-- determine max deliveries by any bowler in each over
max_deliveries_per_over AS (
  SELECT
    match_id,
    innings_no,
    over_id,
    MAX(deliveries_by_this_bowler) AS max_deliveries_by_bowler_in_over
  FROM bowler_delivery_counts
  GROUP BY match_id, innings_no, over_id
),
-- for each over, keep only bowler(s) who delivered the maximum number of deliveries (handles ties)
majority_bowlers_per_over AS (
  SELECT
    b.match_id,
    b.innings_no,
    b.over_id,
    b.bowler_id,
    b.deliveries_by_this_bowler,
    t.total_deliveries_in_over
  FROM bowler_delivery_counts b
  JOIN max_deliveries_per_over m
    ON b.match_id = m.match_id
    AND b.innings_no = m.innings_no
    AND b.over_id = m.over_id
    AND b.deliveries_by_this_bowler = m.max_deliveries_by_bowler_in_over
  JOIN total_deliveries t
    ON b.match_id = t.match_id
    AND b.innings_no = t.innings_no
    AND b.over_id = t.over_id
),
-- combine runs and majority bowler(s) and team_bowling
over_with_bowler_and_team AS (
  SELECT
    o.match_id,
    o.innings_no,
    o.over_id,
    o.runs_conceded_in_over,
    mb.bowler_id,
    td.team_bowling
  FROM over_runs o
  JOIN majority_bowlers_per_over mb
    ON o.match_id = mb.match_id
    AND o.innings_no = mb.innings_no
    AND o.over_id = mb.over_id
  -- get team_bowling from any delivery in that over
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT match_id, innings_no, over_id, team_bowling
    FROM ball_delivery_canonical
    GROUP BY match_id, innings_no, over_id, team_bowling
  ) td
    ON td.match_id = o.match_id
    AND td.innings_no = o.innings_no
    AND td.over_id = o.over_id
),
-- per match+innings find the maximum over runs
max_over_per_innings AS (
  SELECT
    match_id,
    innings_no,
    MAX(runs_conceded_in_over) AS max_runs_in_innings
  FROM over_with_bowler_and_team
  GROUP BY match_id, innings_no
),
-- keep only overs that are the maximum within their match+innings
max_overs_across_matches AS (
  SELECT
    w.match_id,
    w.innings_no,
    w.over_id,
    w.runs_conceded_in_over,
    w.bowler_id,
    w.team_bowling
  FROM over_with_bowler_and_team w
  JOIN max_over_per_innings m
    ON w.match_id = m.match_id
    AND w.innings_no = m.innings_no
    AND w.runs_conceded_in_over = m.max_runs_in_innings
)
SELECT
  p.player_id AS bowler_player_id,
  p.player_name AS player_name,
  mo.match_id,
  m.match_date,
  mo.team_bowling AS team_bowling,
  mo.over_id,
  mo.innings_no,
  mo.runs_conceded_in_over AS runs_conceded_in_that_over
FROM max_overs_across_matches mo
JOIN player p
  ON p.player_id = mo.bowler_id
JOIN "match" m
  ON m.match_id = mo.match_id
ORDER BY
  mo.runs_conceded_in_over DESC,
  m.match_date ASC,
  p.player_id ASC
LIMIT 3

    b.innings_no,
    b.over_id,
    b.ball_id,

  FROM ball_by_ball b

    d.innings_no,

    d.bowler,
    COALESCE(batsman_scored.runs_scored, 0) AS runs_scored,
    COALESCE(extra_runs.extra_runs, 0) AS extra_runs,

  FROM balling_deliveries_canonical d
  LEFT JOIN batsman_scored

    AND batsman_scored.innings_no = d.innings_no
    AND batsman_scored.over_id = d.over_id
    AND batsman_scored.ball_id = d.ball_id

    AND extra_runs.innings_no = d.innings_no
    AND extra_runs.over_id = d.over_id
    AND extra_runs.ball_id = d.ball_id
),
bowler_aggregates_per_player AS (
  SELECT
    d.bowler AS player_id,
    SUM(d.total_runs_conceded_on_ball) AS total_runs_conceded,
    SUM(CASE WHEN w.match_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_wickets_taken
  FROM delivery_runs_extras d
  LEFT JOIN wicket_taken w
    ON w.match_id = d.match_id
    AND w.innings_no = d.innings_no
    AND w.over_id = d.over_id
    AND w.ball_id = d.ball_id

  b.player_id,
  p.player_name,

rows.question: Can you help me find the top 5 countries whose players have the highest average of their individual average runs per match across all seasons?     NULLIF(player.country_name, '') AS country_name
  FROM player

),

  SELECT
    player_match.player_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT player_match.match_id) AS matches_played
  FROM player_match
  GROUP BY player_match.player_id

  SELECT
    b.match_id,
    b.over_id,

    b.striker,
    COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) AS runs_scored

   AND b.over_id = bs.over_id

  JOIN player_matches_count pmc
    ON pmc.player_id = pb.player_id

    ON ptr.player_id = pb.player_id

WITH legislator_terms_canonical AS (
  SELECT
    id_bioguide,
    term_id,
    CASE WHEN trim(term_start) = '' THEN NULL ELSE date(term_start) END AS term_start_date,
    CASE WHEN trim(term_end) = '' THEN NULL ELSE date(term_end) END AS term_end_date,
    state, party, term_number, term_type
  FROM legislators_terms
),
legislators_core AS (
  SELECT
    id_bioguide,
    full_name, first_name, last_name, gender, id_govtrack, id_wikidata
  FROM legislators
),
legislator_first_term AS (
  SELECT
    id_bioguide,
    MIN(term_start_date) AS first_term_start_date,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', MIN(term_start_date)) AS INTEGER) AS first_term_year
  FROM legislator_terms_canonical
  WHERE term_start_date IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY id_bioguide
),
years AS (
  SELECT 31 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 32 UNION ALL SELECT 33 UNION ALL SELECT 34 UNION ALL
  SELECT 35 UNION ALL SELECT 36 UNION ALL SELECT 37 UNION ALL SELECT 38 UNION ALL
  SELECT 39 UNION ALL SELECT 40 UNION ALL SELECT 41 UNION ALL SELECT 42 UNION ALL
  SELECT 43 UNION ALL SELECT 44 UNION ALL SELECT 45 UNION ALL SELECT 46 UNION ALL
  SELECT 47 UNION ALL SELECT 48 UNION ALL SELECT 49
)
SELECT
  y.n AS years_since_first_term,
  COUNT(DISTINCT lft.id_bioguide) AS active_legislator_count
FROM legislator_first_term lft
JOIN legislators_core lc USING (id_bioguide)
CROSS JOIN years y
JOIN legislator_terms_canonical ltc
  ON ltc.id_bioguide = lft.id_bioguide
WHERE
  lc.gender = 'M'
  AND ltc.state = 'LA'
  -- compute the December 31 of the target year (first_term_year + n) and check coverage
  AND date((lft.first_term_year + y.n) || '-12-31') IS NOT NULL
  AND ltc.term_start_date IS NOT NULL
  AND ltc.term_end_date IS NOT NULL
  AND date((lft.first_term_year + y.n) || '-12-31') BETWEEN ltc.term_start_date AND ltc.term_end_date
GROUP BY y.n
ORDER BY y.n

rows.question: Based on the state each female legislator first represented, which state has the highest number of female legislators whose terms included December 31st at any point, and what is that count? Please provide the state's abbreviation.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH first_state AS (
  SELECT lt.id_bioguide,
         lt.state AS first_state
  FROM legislators_terms lt
  JOIN (
    SELECT id_bioguide, MIN(term_number) AS min_term_number
    FROM legislators_terms
    GROUP BY id_bioguide
  ) m ON lt.id_bioguide = m.id_bioguide AND lt.term_number = m.min_term_number
  WHERE lt.state IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(lt.state) <> ''
),
has_dec_31 AS (
  SELECT id_bioguide
  FROM legislators_terms
  WHERE DATE(term_start) IS NOT NULL
    AND DATE(term_end) IS NOT NULL
    AND DATE(term_start) <= DATE(term_end)
    AND (
      -- term spans at least one calendar year boundary (so some YYYY-12-31 is inside)
      CAST(substr(term_end,1,4) AS INTEGER) - CAST(substr(term_start,1,4) AS INTEGER) >= 1
      OR
      -- or the same year and includes that year's 12-31
      (substr(term_start,1,4) = substr(term_end,1,4)
       AND DATE(substr(term_start,1,4) || '-12-31') BETWEEN DATE(term_start) AND DATE(term_end))
    )
  GROUP BY id_bioguide
)
SELECT f.first_state AS state,
       COUNT(DISTINCT l.id_bioguide) AS female_legislator_count
FROM legislators l
JOIN first_state f ON l.id_bioguide = f.id_bioguide
JOIN has_dec_31 d ON l.id_bioguide = d.id_bioguide
WHERE LOWER(TRIM(l.gender)) = 'f' OR LOWER(TRIM(l.gender)) = 'female'
GROUP BY f.first_state
ORDER BY female_legislator_count DESC
LIMIT 1

rows.question: Identify the state abbreviations where, for both male and female legislators, the retention rate remains greater than zero at specific intervals of 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 years after their first term start date. A legislator is considered retained if they are serving on December 31 of the respective year. Only include states where both gender cohorts maintain non-zero retention rates at all six of these time points during the first decade of service.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH legislators_first_terms AS (
  SELECT
    id_bioguide,
    state,
    DATE(term_start) AS term_start_date,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', DATE(term_start)) AS INTEGER) AS first_year
  FROM legislators_terms
  WHERE term_number = 0
    AND state IS NOT NULL
    AND term_start IS NOT NULL
),
legislators_core AS (
  SELECT id_bioguide, gender
  FROM legislators
  WHERE id_bioguide IS NOT NULL
    AND gender IN ('M','F')
),
offsets AS (
  SELECT 0 AS off UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 10
),
legislators_terms_normalized AS (
  SELECT id_bioguide, state,
         DATE(term_start) AS term_start,
         DATE(term_end)   AS term_end
  FROM legislators_terms
  WHERE state IS NOT NULL
    AND term_start IS NOT NULL
    AND term_end IS NOT NULL
),
-- For each legislator's first term baseline and each offset, find if that legislator (with their state)
-- has any term that covers Dec 31 of (first_year + offset)
legislator_serving_at AS (
  SELECT
    ft.state,
    o.off AS offset_years,
    lc.gender,
    ft.id_bioguide
  FROM legislators_first_terms ft
  CROSS JOIN offsets o
  JOIN legislators_core lc ON lc.id_bioguide = ft.id_bioguide
  JOIN legislators_terms_normalized lt
    ON lt.id_bioguide = ft.id_bioguide
       AND lt.state = ft.state
       AND DATE(ft.first_year || '-' || '12' || '-' || '31', '+' || o.off || ' years') = DATE((ft.first_year + o.off) || '-12-31') -- kept for clarity but SQLite will evaluate expression below
       -- check coverage: term_start <= Dec31(first_year+off) <= term_end
       AND lt.term_start <= DATE((ft.first_year + o.off) || '-12-31')
       AND lt.term_end   >= DATE((ft.first_year + o.off) || '-12-31')
  GROUP BY ft.state, o.off, lc.gender, ft.id_bioguide
),
state_offset_gender_presence AS (
  SELECT
    state,
    offset_years,
    MAX(CASE WHEN gender = 'M' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_m,
    MAX(CASE WHEN gender = 'F' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_f
  FROM legislator_serving_at
  GROUP BY state, offset_years
)
SELECT state
FROM state_offset_gender_presence
GROUP BY state
HAVING SUM(has_m) = 6 AND SUM(has_f) = 6
ORDER BY state

rows.question: For alien data, how many of the top 10 states by alien population have a higher percentage of friendly aliens than hostile aliens, with an average alien age exceeding 200?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH aliens_base_rows AS (
  SELECT
    id,
    first_name,
    last_name,
    state,
    age,
    birth_year,
    favorite_food,
    feeding_frequency,
    aggressive,
    current_location,
    country
  FROM alien_data
),
aliens_state_aggregates AS (
  SELECT
    state,
    COUNT(*) AS population_count,
    COUNT(age) AS age_count,
    CASE WHEN COUNT(age) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE AVG(age) END AS age_avg,
    SUM(CASE WHEN aggressive = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS aggressive_friendly_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN aggressive = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS aggressive_hostile_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN aggressive IN (0,1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS aggression_known_count
  FROM aliens_base_rows
  GROUP BY state
),
aliens_state_metrics_for_comparison AS (
  SELECT
    a.state AS state,
    a.population_count AS population_count,
    a.aggression_known_count AS aggression_known_count,
    a.aggressive_friendly_count AS aggressive_friendly_count,
    a.aggressive_hostile_count AS aggressive_hostile_count,
    CASE
      WHEN a.aggression_known_count > 0 THEN (CAST(a.aggressive_friendly_count AS REAL) / a.aggression_known_count) * 100.0
      ELSE NULL
    END AS percentage_friendly,
    CASE
      WHEN a.aggression_known_count > 0 THEN (CAST(a.aggressive_hostile_count AS REAL) / a.aggression_known_count) * 100.0
      ELSE NULL
    END AS percentage_hostile,
    a.age_count AS age_count,
    a.age_avg AS age_avg
  FROM aliens_state_aggregates a
)
SELECT
  SUM(CASE WHEN m.percentage_friendly > m.percentage_hostile AND m.age_avg > 200 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_of_states_meeting_criteria,
  json_group_array(json_object('state', t.state, 'population_count', t.population_count)) AS top_10_states_population_list
FROM (
  SELECT state, population_count
  FROM aliens_state_metrics_for_comparison
  ORDER BY population_count DESC, state ASC
  LIMIT 10
) AS t
JOIN aliens_state_metrics_for_comparison AS m
  ON t.state = m.state

rows.question: Considering all races where pit stop data is available, and focusing on instances when a driver was not behind another car on the previous lap but is behind on the current lap (accounting for retirements, pit-stop entries, pit-stop exits, and race starts), how many times has each type of overtake occurred in Formula 1?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH valid_races AS (
  SELECT race_id
  FROM races_ext
  WHERE is_pit_data_available IN ('1','t','true','True','TRUE','yes','Y','y','on','1.0')
), 
lp AS (
  SELECT race_id, driver_id, lap, position
  FROM lap_positions
  WHERE race_id IN (SELECT race_id FROM valid_races)
    AND lap IS NOT NULL
    AND position IS NOT NULL
),
pairs AS (
  SELECT
    cur.race_id,
    cur.lap AS lap,
    prev.lap AS prev_lap,
    cur.driver_id AS overtaker_id,
    cur.position AS overtaker_pos,
    prev.position AS overtaker_prev_pos,
    other.driver_id AS overtaken_id,
    cur_other.position AS overtaken_pos,
    prev_other.position AS overtaken_prev_pos
  FROM lp cur
  JOIN lp prev
    ON cur.race_id = prev.race_id
   AND cur.driver_id = prev.driver_id
   AND cur.lap = prev.lap + 1
  JOIN lp other
    ON cur.race_id = other.race_id
   AND cur.lap = other.lap
  JOIN lp prev_other
    ON prev.race_id = prev_other.race_id
   AND prev.lap = prev_other.lap
   AND other.driver_id = prev_other.driver_id
  JOIN lp cur_other
    ON cur.race_id = cur_other.race_id
   AND cur.lap = cur_other.lap
   AND other.driver_id = cur_other.driver_id
  WHERE cur.driver_id <> other.driver_id
),
overtakes AS (
  SELECT
    p.race_id,
    p.lap,
    p.prev_lap,
    p.overtaker_id,
    p.overtaken_id
  FROM pairs p
  WHERE p.overtaker_prev_pos IS NOT NULL
    AND p.overtaken_prev_pos IS NOT NULL
    AND p.overtaker_pos IS NOT NULL
    AND p.overtaken_pos IS NOT NULL
    -- not behind on previous lap (numeric: higher value = further back). So not behind means prev_overtaker_pos <= prev_overtaken_pos
    AND p.overtaker_prev_pos <= p.overtaken_prev_pos
    -- behind on current lap: overtaker_pos > overtaken_pos
    AND p.overtaker_pos > p.overtaken_pos
    -- consider only racing laps (allow prev_lap = 0 so lap = 1 can capture race start changes)
    AND p.lap > 0
),
rets AS (
  SELECT race_id, driver_id, lap
  FROM retirements
  WHERE race_id IN (SELECT race_id FROM valid_races)
    AND lap IS NOT NULL
    AND lap <> ''
),
ps AS (
  SELECT race_id, driver_id, stop AS lap
  FROM pit_stops
  WHERE race_id IN (SELECT race_id FROM valid_races)
    AND stop IS NOT NULL
),
classified AS (
  SELECT
    o.race_id,
    o.lap,
    o.overtaker_id,
    o.overtaken_id,
    CASE
      WHEN EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM rets r
        WHERE r.race_id = o.race_id
          AND r.driver_id = o.overtaken_id
          AND CAST(r.lap AS INTEGER) = CAST(o.lap AS INTEGER)
      ) THEN 'R'
      WHEN EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM ps p
        WHERE p.race_id = o.race_id
          AND p.driver_id = o.overtaken_id
          AND CAST(p.lap AS INTEGER) = CAST(o.lap AS INTEGER)
      )
      OR EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM ps p2
        WHERE p2.race_id = o.race_id
          AND p2.driver_id = o.overtaken_id
          AND CAST(p2.lap AS INTEGER) = CAST(o.prev_lap AS INTEGER)
      )
      THEN 'P'
      ELSE 'O'
    END AS label
  FROM overtakes o
)
SELECT label, COUNT(*) AS count
FROM classified
GROUP BY label

rows.question: In the first five laps of the race, how many overtakes occurred in each category—retirements, pit stops, start-related overtakes, and standard on-track passes?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH race_pit_stops AS (
  SELECT
    race_id,
    driver_id,
    lap
  FROM pit_stops
),
race_retirements AS (
  SELECT
    retirements.race_id AS race_id,
    retirements.driver_id AS driver_id,
    CAST(retirements.lap AS INTEGER) AS lap
  FROM retirements
  WHERE retirements.lap IS NOT NULL
),
first_lap_position_changes AS (
  SELECT
    res.race_id,
    res.driver_id,
    res.grid AS grid_start,
    COALESCE(lp.position, rlt.position) AS first_lap_position,
    (COALESCE(lp.position, rlt.position) - res.grid) AS position_change
  FROM results res
  LEFT JOIN lap_positions lp
    ON res.race_id = lp.race_id
    AND res.driver_id = lp.driver_id
    AND lp.lap = 1
  LEFT JOIN lap_times_ext rlt
    ON res.race_id = rlt.race_id
    AND res.driver_id = rlt.driver_id
    AND rlt.lap = 1
),
overtake_rows AS (
  -- use lap_times_ext rows as proxy for overtakes per driver per lap
  SELECT
    lte.race_id,
    lte.driver_id,
    lte.lap
  FROM lap_times_ext lte
  WHERE lte.lap BETWEEN 1 AND 5
)
SELECT
  SUM(CASE WHEN rr.driver_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS retirements_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN rr.driver_id IS NULL
           AND rps.driver_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS pit_stops_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN rr.driver_id IS NULL
           AND rps.driver_id IS NULL
           AND flpc.driver_id IS NOT NULL
           AND o.lap = 1
           AND flpc.position_change > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS start_related_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN rr.driver_id IS NULL
           AND rps.driver_id IS NULL
           AND NOT (flpc.driver_id IS NOT NULL AND o.lap = 1 AND flpc.position_change > 0)
           THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS standard_on_track_count
FROM overtake_rows o
LEFT JOIN race_retirements rr
  ON rr.race_id = o.race_id
  AND rr.driver_id = o.driver_id
  AND rr.lap = o.lap
LEFT JOIN race_pit_stops rps
  ON rps.race_id = o.race_id
  AND rps.driver_id = o.driver_id
  AND rps.lap IN (o.lap, o.lap - 1)
LEFT JOIN first_lap_position_changes flpc
  ON flpc.race_id = o.race_id
  AND flpc.driver_id = o.driver_id

rows.question: In Formula 1 seasons since 2001, considering only drivers who scored points in a season, which five constructors have had the most seasons where their drivers scored the fewest total points among all point-scoring drivers in that season?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH race_results_with_season AS (
  SELECT
    r.result_id,
    r.race_id,
    ra.year,
    r.driver_id,
    r.constructor_id,
    r.points
  FROM results r
  JOIN races ra ON r.race_id = ra.race_id
  WHERE ra.year >= 2001
),
driver_season_points AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    driver_id,
    SUM(points) AS season_total_points
  FROM race_results_with_season
  GROUP BY year, driver_id
),
driver_season_constructors AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    driver_id,
    constructor_id
  FROM race_results_with_season
  GROUP BY year, driver_id, constructor_id
),
year_min_positive AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    MIN(season_total_points) AS min_points
  FROM driver_season_points
  WHERE season_total_points > 0
  GROUP BY year
)
SELECT
  c.constructor_id,
  c.name AS constructor_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT dsp.year) AS seasons_with_lowest_point_scoring_driver
FROM driver_season_points dsp
JOIN year_min_positive ymp
  ON dsp.year = ymp.year
  AND dsp.season_total_points = ymp.min_points
  -- dsp.season_total_points > 0 ensured by ymp
JOIN driver_season_constructors dsc
  ON dsp.year = dsc.year
  AND dsp.driver_id = dsc.driver_id
JOIN constructors c
  ON dsc.constructor_id = c.constructor_id
GROUP BY c.constructor_id, c.name
ORDER BY seasons_with_lowest_point_scoring_driver DESC, c.constructor_id ASC
LIMIT 5

rows.question: For each year, which driver and which constructor scored the most points? I want the full name of each driver.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH race_years AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(re.race_id, r.race_id) AS race_id,
         COALESCE(re.year, r.year) AS year
  FROM races r
  LEFT JOIN races_ext re ON r.race_id = re.race_id
  UNION
  -- include races present only in races_ext
  SELECT re.race_id, re.year
  FROM races_ext re
  LEFT JOIN races r ON r.race_id = re.race_id
  WHERE r.race_id IS NULL
),
-- aggregated driver points per year (prefer driver_standings_ext when available by including both sources)
drivers_per_year AS (
  SELECT ry.year, ds.driver_id, SUM(ds.points) AS driver_points
  FROM race_years ry
  JOIN driver_standings ds ON ds.race_id = ry.race_id
  GROUP BY ry.year, ds.driver_id
  UNION ALL
  SELECT ry.year, dse.driver_id, SUM(dse.points) AS driver_points
  FROM race_years ry
  JOIN driver_standings_ext dse ON dse.race_id = ry.race_id
  GROUP BY ry.year, dse.driver_id
),
-- combine aggregates for same (year,driver) coming from both tables
drivers_combined AS (
  SELECT year, driver_id, SUM(driver_points) AS driver_points
  FROM drivers_per_year
  GROUP BY year, driver_id
),
dmax AS (
  SELECT year, driver_id, driver_points
  FROM (
    SELECT year, driver_id, driver_points,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY driver_points DESC) AS rn
    FROM drivers_combined
  ) t
  WHERE rn = 1
),
-- aggregated constructor points per year (include both tables if present)
constructors_per_year AS (
  SELECT ry.year, cs.constructor_id, SUM(cs.points) AS constructor_points
  FROM race_years ry
  JOIN constructor_standings cs ON cs.race_id = ry.race_id
  GROUP BY ry.year, cs.constructor_id
  UNION ALL
  SELECT ry.year, cse.constructor_id, SUM(cse.points) AS constructor_points
  FROM race_years ry
  JOIN constructor_standings cse ON cse.race_id = ry.race_id
  GROUP BY ry.year, cse.constructor_id
),
-- (Note: schema shows only constructor_standings; above UNION ALL is harmless if duplicate)
constructors_combined AS (
  SELECT year, constructor_id, SUM(constructor_points) AS constructor_points
  FROM constructors_per_year
  GROUP BY year, constructor_id
),
cmax AS (
  SELECT year, constructor_id, constructor_points
  FROM (
    SELECT year, constructor_id, constructor_points,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY constructor_points DESC) AS rn
    FROM constructors_combined
  ) t
  WHERE rn = 1
)
SELECT
  dmax.year,
  COALESCE(de.full_name, TRIM(COALESCE(d.forename, '') || ' ' || COALESCE(d.surname, ''))) AS driver_full_name,
  dmax.driver_points,
  COALESCE(ce.name, c.name) AS constructor_name,
  cmax.constructor_points
FROM dmax
JOIN cmax ON cmax.year = dmax.year
LEFT JOIN drivers_ext de ON de.driver_id = dmax.driver_id
LEFT JOIN drivers d ON d.driver_id = dmax.driver_id
LEFT JOIN constructors_ext ce ON ce.constructor_id = cmax.constructor_id
LEFT JOIN constructors c ON c.constructor_id = cmax.constructor_id
ORDER BY dmax.year ASC

rows.question: Using only the data from the ‘results’ table, find the three years in which the sum of the highest total points earned by any driver and the highest total points earned by any constructor in that year (both calculated by summing up points from the ‘results’ table) is smallest, and list those three years in order of ascending total.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH results_with_race_year AS (
  SELECT
    r.result_id,
    r.race_id,
    races.year,
    r.driver_id,
    r.constructor_id,
    r.points
  FROM results AS r
  LEFT JOIN races ON r.race_id = races.race_id
  WHERE races.year IS NOT NULL
),
driver_yearly_points AS (
  SELECT
    rwry.year AS year,
    rwry.driver_id AS driver_id,
    SUM(COALESCE(rwry.points, 0.0)) AS driver_total_points
  FROM results_with_race_year rwry
  GROUP BY rwry.year, rwry.driver_id
),
constructor_yearly_points AS (
  SELECT
    r.year AS year,
    r.constructor_id AS constructor_id,
    SUM(COALESCE(r.points, 0.0)) AS constructor_total_points
  FROM results_with_race_year r
  GROUP BY r.year, r.constructor_id
)
SELECT
  dyp.year AS year,
  MAX(dyp.driver_total_points) AS driver_max_points,

FROM driver_yearly_points dyp
JOIN constructor_yearly_points cyp USING (year)
GROUP BY dyp.year
ORDER BY driver_plus_constructor_max_points ASC

rows.question: Which constructors had the top 3 combined points from their best driver and team, and in which years did they achieve them?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH
-- derive team (constructor) season points per year from constructor_standings joined to races to get year
constructor_year_points AS (
  SELECT
    cs.constructor_id,
    r.year,
    SUM(cs.points) AS team_points
  FROM constructor_standings cs
  JOIN races r ON cs.race_id = r.race_id
  GROUP BY cs.constructor_id, r.year
),
-- driver season points per driver per year from driver_standings joined to races
driver_year_points AS (
  SELECT
    ds.driver_id,
    r.year,
    SUM(ds.points) AS driver_points
  FROM driver_standings ds
  JOIN races r ON ds.race_id = r.race_id
  GROUP BY ds.driver_id, r.year
),
-- map drivers to constructors per year using results table (drivers who drove for constructor that year)
driver_constructor_year AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    res.constructor_id,
    res.driver_id,
    r.year
  FROM results res
  JOIN races r ON res.race_id = r.race_id
  WHERE res.constructor_id IS NOT NULL
),
-- combine to get for each constructor-year the drivers (with their season points) who drove for that constructor that year
best_driver_per_constructor_year AS (
  SELECT
    dcy.constructor_id,
    dcy.year,
    dcy.driver_id,
    dyp.driver_points
  FROM driver_constructor_year dcy
  JOIN driver_year_points dyp
    ON dcy.driver_id = dyp.driver_id
   AND dcy.year = dyp.year
),
-- pick max driver_points per constructor-year, tie-break by lowest driver_id
best_driver_ranked AS (
  SELECT
    constructor_id,
    year,
    driver_id,
    driver_points,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY constructor_id, year
      ORDER BY driver_points DESC, driver_id ASC
    ) AS rn
  FROM best_driver_per_constructor_year
),
best_driver_final AS (
  SELECT constructor_id, year, driver_id, driver_points
  FROM best_driver_ranked
  WHERE rn = 1
),
-- combine with team points; require both present (INNER JOIN)
constructor_year_combined AS (
  SELECT
    bdf.year,
    bdf.constructor_id,
    bdf.driver_id AS driver_id_of_best_driver,
    bdf.driver_points,
    cyp.team_points,
    (bdf.driver_points + cyp.team_points) AS combined_points
  FROM best_driver_final bdf
  JOIN constructor_year_points cyp
    ON bdf.constructor_id = cyp.constructor_id
   AND bdf.year = cyp.year
),
-- rank constructors within each year by combined_points, tie-breaks: higher team_points, then lower constructor_id
constructor_year_ranked AS (
  SELECT
    cyc.*,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY cyc.year
      ORDER BY cyc.combined_points DESC, cyc.team_points DESC, cyc.constructor_id ASC
