rows.question: Among Formula 1 drivers who raced during the 1950s, which drivers completed a season in that decade with the same constructor in both the first and the last race they participated in, while also taking part in at least two distinct race rounds during that season?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH drives_by_year_driver_round AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    driver_id,
    constructor_id,
    first_round,
    last_round,
    is_first_drive_of_season,
    is_final_drive_of_season,
    drive_id
  FROM drives
),
driver_season_round_summary AS (
  SELECT
    d.year,
    d.driver_id,
    MIN(d.first_round) AS first_round,
    MAX(d.last_round) AS last_round,
    COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(d.first_round, d.last_round, d.drive_id)) AS distinct_rounds_cnt
  FROM drives_by_year_driver_round d
  GROUP BY d.year, d.driver_id
),
-- get the constructor associated with the actual first round (the drive row that has that first_round)
first_constructor AS (
  SELECT
    s.year,
    s.driver_id,
    d.constructor_id
  FROM driver_season_round_summary s
  JOIN drives_by_year_driver_round d
    ON d.year = s.year
   AND d.driver_id = s.driver_id
   -- choose the drive row that contains the season first_round (it may be in first_round column)
   AND (d.first_round = s.first_round OR d.last_round = s.first_round)
  -- if multiple drives match the same first_round, prefer a non-null constructor_id; leave duplicates handled by aggregation below
  GROUP BY s.year, s.driver_id
  HAVING MAX(d.constructor_id) IS NOT NULL
),
-- get the constructor associated with the actual last round
last_constructor AS (
  SELECT
    s.year,
    s.driver_id,
    d.constructor_id
  FROM driver_season_round_summary s
  JOIN drives_by_year_driver_round d
    ON d.year = s.year
   AND d.driver_id = s.driver_id
   AND (d.first_round = s.last_round OR d.last_round = s.last_round)
  GROUP BY s.year, s.driver_id
  HAVING MAX(d.constructor_id) IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  s.year,
  s.driver_id,
  COALESCE(d.driver_ref, de.full_name) AS driver_name,
  fc.constructor_id AS constructor_id,
  COALESCE(c.constructor_ref, ce.constructor_ref, ce.name) AS constructor_ref_or_name,
  s.first_round,
  s.last_round,
  s.distinct_rounds_cnt AS number_of_distinct_rounds_participated
FROM driver_season_round_summary s
JOIN first_constructor fc
  ON fc.year = s.year AND fc.driver_id = s.driver_id
JOIN last_constructor lc
  ON lc.year = s.year AND lc.driver_id = s.driver_id
  AND lc.constructor_id = fc.constructor_id
LEFT JOIN drivers d
  ON d.driver_id = s.driver_id
LEFT JOIN drivers_ext de
  ON de.driver_id = s.driver_id
LEFT JOIN constructors c
  ON c.constructor_id = fc.constructor_id
LEFT JOIN constructors_ext ce
  ON ce.constructor_id = fc.constructor_id
WHERE s.year BETWEEN 1950 AND 1959
  AND s.distinct_rounds_cnt >= 2
  AND fc.constructor_id IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY s.year ASC, s.driver_id ASC

rows.question: Calculate the overall average first round and average last round of races missed by Formula 1 drivers across all years. Include only drivers who missed fewer than three races in a given year and who switched teams between their appearances immediately before and after their hiatus (i.e., the constructor ID for the race right before their first missed race must be different from the constructor ID for the race right after their last missed race in that year). Do not group results by year; return just the overall averages across the entire dataset.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH drives_driver_year_round_rows AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    driver_id,
    drive_id,
    constructor_id,
    CAST(NULLIF(first_round, '') AS INTEGER) AS first_round,
    CAST(NULLIF(last_round, '') AS INTEGER) AS last_round
  FROM drives
),
driver_year_adjacent_round_appearances AS (
  SELECT
    d.year,
    d.driver_id,
    d.first_round,
    d.last_round,
    (d.first_round - 1) AS prior_round,
    (SELECT dd.constructor_id
     FROM drives_driver_year_round_rows dd
     WHERE dd.year = d.year
       AND dd.driver_id = d.driver_id
       AND dd.first_round <= (d.first_round - 1)
       AND dd.last_round  >= (d.first_round - 1)
     LIMIT 1) AS prior_constructor_id,
    (d.last_round + 1) AS next_round,
    (SELECT dd2.constructor_id
     FROM drives_driver_year_round_rows dd2
     WHERE dd2.year = d.year
       AND dd2.driver_id = d.driver_id
       AND dd2.first_round <= (d.last_round + 1)
       AND dd2.last_round  >= (d.last_round + 1)
     LIMIT 1) AS next_constructor_id
  FROM drives_driver_year_round_rows d
  WHERE d.first_round IS NOT NULL AND d.last_round IS NOT NULL
),
driver_year_short_missed_blocks AS (
  SELECT
    d.year,
    d.driver_id,
    d.first_round,
    d.last_round,
    (d.last_round - d.first_round + 1) AS block_length,
    d.prior_constructor_id,
    d.next_constructor_id
  FROM driver_year_adjacent_round_appearances d
  WHERE (d.last_round - d.first_round + 1) < 3
    AND d.prior_constructor_id IS NOT NULL
    AND d.next_constructor_id IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  AVG(first_round) AS avg_first_missed_round,
  AVG(last_round)  AS avg_last_missed_round
FROM driver_year_short_missed_blocks
WHERE prior_constructor_id != next_constructor_id

rows.question: Provide the full names of drivers who have been overtaken on track more times than they have overtaken others on track during race laps, excluding position changes due to pit stops (both at pit entry and exit), retirements, or position changes that occurred during the first lap of a race (considered as start movements).
rows.pred_sql:
WITH lap_positions_per_driver_per_lap AS (
  SELECT
    race_id,
    driver_id,
    lap,
    position,
    lap_type
  FROM lap_positions
),
driver_identity_canonical AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(de.driver_id, d.driver_id) AS driver_id,
    COALESCE(de.full_name,
             TRIM(
               COALESCE(d.forename, '') ||
               CASE WHEN d.forename IS NOT NULL AND d.surname IS NOT NULL THEN ' ' ELSE '' END ||
               COALESCE(d.surname, '')
             )
    ) AS full_name,
    COALESCE(de.driver_ref, d.driver_ref) AS driver_ref,
    COALESCE(de.number, d.number) AS number,
    COALESCE(de.nationality, d.nationality) AS nationality
  FROM drivers d
  LEFT JOIN drivers_ext de ON d.driver_id = de.driver_id
),
pit_and_retirement_flags_per_lap AS (
  SELECT
    lp.race_id,
    lp.driver_id,
    lp.lap,
    CASE WHEN ps.stop IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_pit_stop,
    CASE WHEN r.lap IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_retirement
  FROM lap_positions_per_driver_per_lap lp
  LEFT JOIN pit_stops ps
    ON ps.race_id = lp.race_id
   AND ps.driver_id = lp.driver_id
   AND ps.lap = lp.lap
  LEFT JOIN retirements r
    ON r.race_id = lp.race_id
   AND r.driver_id = lp.driver_id
   AND CAST(r.lap AS INTEGER) = lp.lap
)
SELECT
  agg.driver_id,
  dic.full_name,
  agg.overtaken_count,
  agg.overtake_count,
  (agg.overtaken_count - agg.overtake_count) AS net_overtakes
FROM (
  SELECT
    curr.driver_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN curr.position > prev.position THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS overtaken_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN curr.position < prev.position THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS overtake_count
  FROM lap_positions_per_driver_per_lap curr
  JOIN lap_positions_per_driver_per_lap prev
    ON curr.race_id = prev.race_id
   AND curr.driver_id = prev.driver_id
   AND curr.lap = prev.lap + 1
  LEFT JOIN pit_and_retirement_flags_per_lap flags
    ON curr.race_id = flags.race_id
   AND curr.driver_id = flags.driver_id
   AND curr.lap = flags.lap
  WHERE curr.lap <> 1
    AND (flags.has_pit_stop IS NULL OR flags.has_pit_stop = 0)
    AND (flags.has_retirement IS NULL OR flags.has_retirement = 0)
  GROUP BY curr.driver_id
) AS agg
JOIN driver_identity_canonical dic
  ON agg.driver_id = dic.driver_id
WHERE (agg.overtaken_count - agg.overtake_count) > 0
ORDER BY net_overtakes DESC, overtaken_count DESC, agg.driver_id ASC

WITH geolocation_canonical AS (
  SELECT
    geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
    CAST(geolocation_lat AS FLOAT) AS geolocation_lat,
    CAST(geolocation_lng AS FLOAT) AS geolocation_lng,
    geolocation_city,
    geolocation_state
  FROM olist_geolocation
),
geolocation_ordered_with_prev AS (
  SELECT
    g.geolocation_state,
    g.geolocation_city,
    g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
    g.geolocation_lat,
    g.geolocation_lng,
    LAG(g.geolocation_state) OVER (ORDER BY g.geolocation_state, g.geolocation_city, g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix, g.geolocation_lat, g.geolocation_lng) AS prev_geolocation_state,
    LAG(g.geolocation_city)  OVER (ORDER BY g.geolocation_state, g.geolocation_city, g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix, g.geolocation_lat, g.geolocation_lng) AS prev_geolocation_city,
    LAG(g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix) OVER (ORDER BY g.geolocation_state, g.geolocation_city, g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix, g.geolocation_lat, g.geolocation_lng) AS prev_geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
    LAG(g.geolocation_lat)   OVER (ORDER BY g.geolocation_state, g.geolocation_city, g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix, g.geolocation_lat, g.geolocation_lng) AS prev_geolocation_lat,
    LAG(g.geolocation_lng)   OVER (ORDER BY g.geolocation_state, g.geolocation_city, g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix, g.geolocation_lat, g.geolocation_lng) AS prev_geolocation_lng
  FROM geolocation_canonical g
  WHERE g.geolocation_lat IS NOT NULL AND g.geolocation_lng IS NOT NULL
),
geolocation_pairs_distance_components AS (
  SELECT
    prev_geolocation_state,
    prev_geolocation_city,
    prev_geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
    prev_geolocation_lat,
    prev_geolocation_lng,
    geolocation_state,
    geolocation_city,
    geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
    geolocation_lat,
    geolocation_lng,
    (prev_geolocation_lat * 3.141592653589793 / 180.0) AS prev_lat_rad,
    (prev_geolocation_lng * 3.141592653589793 / 180.0) AS prev_lng_rad,
    (geolocation_lat * 3.141592653589793 / 180.0) AS lat_rad,
    (geolocation_lng * 3.141592653589793 / 180.0) AS lng_rad
  FROM geolocation_ordered_with_prev
  WHERE prev_geolocation_lat IS NOT NULL AND prev_geolocation_lng IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  prev_geolocation_state AS geolocation_state_a,
  prev_geolocation_city  AS geolocation_city_a,
  prev_geolocation_zip_code_prefix AS geolocation_zip_code_prefix_a,
  prev_geolocation_lat   AS geolocation_lat_a,
  prev_geolocation_lng   AS geolocation_lng_a,
  geolocation_state      AS geolocation_state_b,
  geolocation_city       AS geolocation_city_b,
  geolocation_zip_code_prefix AS geolocation_zip_code_prefix_b,
  geolocation_lat        AS geolocation_lat_b,
  geolocation_lng        AS geolocation_lng_b,
  6371.0 * acos(
    CASE
      WHEN cos(prev_lat_rad)*cos(lat_rad)*cos(lng_rad - prev_lng_rad) + sin(prev_lat_rad)*sin(lat_rad) > 1 THEN 1
      WHEN cos(prev_lat_rad)*cos(lat_rad)*cos(lng_rad - prev_lng_rad) + sin(prev_lat_rad)*sin(lat_rad) < -1 THEN -1
      ELSE cos(prev_lat_rad)*cos(lat_rad)*cos(lng_rad - prev_lng_rad) + sin(prev_lat_rad)*sin(lat_rad)
    END
  ) AS distance_km
FROM geolocation_pairs_distance_components
ORDER BY distance_km DESC
LIMIT 1

  SELECT packaging_id, contains_id, qty FROM packaging_relations
),
-- identify leaf packaging ids (those that never appear as packaging_id)
leaf_packaging AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT contains_id AS id
  FROM packaging_relations_raw
  WHERE contains_id NOT IN (SELECT packaging_id FROM packaging_relations_raw)
),
-- recursive expansion: for each top-level packaging_id that appears as a container, expand to leaf items with multiplicative qty
expanded AS (
  -- base: direct children of a top-level container
  SELECT
    pr.packaging_id AS top_id,
    pr.contains_id AS leaf_id,
    pr.qty AS qty_mult
  FROM packaging_relations_raw pr

  UNION ALL

  -- recursive: if the child is itself a container, expand further
  SELECT
    e.top_id,
    pr.contains_id AS leaf_id,
    e.qty_mult * pr.qty AS qty_mult
  FROM expanded e
  JOIN packaging_relations_raw pr
    ON e.leaf_id = pr.packaging_id
),
-- keep only expansions that end at leaf packaging ids
expanded_to_leaves AS (
  SELECT top_id, leaf_id, qty_mult
  FROM expanded
  WHERE leaf_id IN (SELECT id FROM leaf_packaging)
),
-- sum total leaf quantities per top-level packaging_id
per_top AS (
  SELECT top_id AS packaging_id, SUM(qty_mult) AS total_qty
  FROM expanded_to_leaves
  GROUP BY top_id
)
-- average across all packaging_id values that appear as containers
SELECT AVG(total_qty) AS average_total_quantity
FROM per_top

rows.question: Which top-level packaging containers, meaning those not contained within any other packaging, have any item for which the total quantity accumulated across all nested levels in the hierarchy exceeds 500, and what are the names of both these containers and the corresponding items?

WITH RECURSIVE
packaging_rows AS (
  SELECT id AS packaging_id, name AS packaging_name FROM packaging
),
packaging_relations_raw AS (
  SELECT packaging_id AS container_id, contains_id AS contained_id, qty FROM packaging_relations
),
-- recursive expansion: for every starting container (root_container_id) traverse containment links,
-- accumulating the multiplicative qty along each path
packaging_containment_recursive AS (
  -- base: direct containment
  SELECT
    container_id AS root_container_id,
    contained_id,
    qty AS path_multiplier,
    1 AS path_length,
    printf('%d', container_id) || '>' || printf('%d', contained_id) AS path_via
  FROM packaging_relations_raw

  UNION ALL

  -- recursive step: extend paths by one containment link
  SELECT
    r.root_container_id,
    pr.contained_id,
    r.path_multiplier * pr.qty AS path_multiplier,
    r.path_length + 1 AS path_length,
    r.path_via || '>' || printf('%d', pr.contained_id) AS path_via
  FROM packaging_containment_recursive r
  JOIN packaging_relations_raw pr
    ON pr.container_id = r.contained_id
)
SELECT
  r.root_container_id AS top_level_packaging_id,
  pr_top.packaging_name AS top_level_packaging_name,
  r.contained_id AS contained_item_id,
  pr_cont.packaging_name AS contained_item_name,
  SUM(r.path_multiplier) AS total_accumulated_qty
FROM packaging_containment_recursive r
JOIN packaging_rows pr_top
  ON pr_top.packaging_id = r.root_container_id
JOIN packaging_rows pr_cont
  ON pr_cont.packaging_id = r.contained_id
WHERE r.path_length >= 1
  -- only consider root containers that are not themselves contained by any other packaging
  AND r.root_container_id NOT IN (SELECT contained_id FROM packaging_relations_raw)
GROUP BY
  r.root_container_id,
  pr_top.packaging_name,
  r.contained_id,
  pr_cont.packaging_name
HAVING SUM(r.path_multiplier) > 500
ORDER BY
  r.root_container_id,
  total_accumulated_qty DESC

    ol.order_id,
    ol.product_id,

    o.ordered,
    o.delivery,
    o.customer_id
  FROM orderlines ol
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = ol.order_id
  WHERE ol.qty > 0
    AND o.ordered IS NOT NULL
),
inventory_lots_with_purchase AS (
  SELECT
    i.id AS inventory_id,
    i.location_id,
    i.product_id,
    i.purchase_id,
    i.qty AS inventory_qty,
    p.purchased
  FROM inventory i
  JOIN purchases p ON i.purchase_id = p.id
  WHERE i.qty > 0
    AND p.purchased IS NOT NULL
),
-- For each orderline and each inventory lot of the same product, compute cumulative inventory before that lot
pairs AS (
  SELECT
    ol.orderline_id,
    il.inventory_id,
    il.inventory_qty,
    ol.orderline_qty,
    il.purchased,
    -- cumulative sum of inventory_qty for this product up to but excluding this inventory lot, ordered FIFO (purchased ASC, inventory_qty ASC, inventory_id ASC)
    COALESCE(
      SUM(il2.inventory_qty) OVER (
        PARTITION BY ol.orderline_id
        ORDER BY il2.purchased, il2.inventory_qty, il2.inventory_id
        ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
      ), 0
    ) AS consumed_before
  FROM orderlines_positive_qty_with_order ol
  JOIN inventory_lots_with_purchase il
    ON il.product_id = ol.product_id
  -- il2 alias used by window; include same set via another reference to inventory_lots_with_purchase to ensure window frames correctly
  JOIN inventory_lots_with_purchase il2
    ON il2.product_id = ol.product_id
  GROUP BY
    ol.orderline_id,
    il.inventory_id,
    il.inventory_qty,
    ol.orderline_qty,
    il.purchased,
    il2.inventory_id,
    il2.inventory_qty,
    il2.purchased
),
-- Determine how much is consumed from each lot for the orderline using FIFO clamping
per_pair_consumed AS (
  SELECT
    orderline_id,
    inventory_id,
    inventory_qty,
    orderline_qty,
    purchased,
    consumed_before,
    CASE
      WHEN (orderline_qty - consumed_before) <= 0 THEN 0
      WHEN (orderline_qty - consumed_before) >= inventory_qty THEN inventory_qty
      ELSE (orderline_qty - consumed_before)
    END AS consumed
  FROM pairs
),
-- Sum consumed per orderline (picked quantity)
picked_by_orderline AS (
  SELECT
    orderline_id,
    COALESCE(SUM(consumed), 0) AS picked_qty
  FROM per_pair_consumed
  GROUP BY orderline_id
)
SELECT

  AVG(

  ) AS avg_pick_pct
FROM products_basic p
JOIN orderlines_positive_qty_with_order ol
  ON ol.product_id = p.product_id
LEFT JOIN picked_by_orderline pb
  ON pb.orderline_id = ol.orderline_id

ORDER BY p.product_name ASC

WITH monthly_product_sales AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    mth,
    COALESCE(qty, 0) AS qty
  FROM monthly_sales
  WHERE mth IS NOT NULL
),
product_12m_centered_moving_avg_windows AS (
  SELECT
    m.product_id AS product_id,
    m.mth AS target_mth,
    w.window_type AS window_type,
    w.window_start_mth AS window_start_mth,
    w.window_end_mth AS window_end_mth,
    SUM(s.qty) AS window_qty_sum,
    COUNT(s.mth) AS window_months_count
  FROM monthly_product_sales m
  JOIN (
    SELECT
      m2.product_id,
      m2.mth AS target_mth,
      'left5_right6' AS window_type,
      date(m2.mth, '-5 months') AS window_start_mth,
      date(m2.mth, '+6 months') AS window_end_mth
    FROM monthly_product_sales m2
    UNION ALL
    SELECT
      m3.product_id,
      m3.mth AS target_mth,
      'left6_right5' AS window_type,
      date(m3.mth, '-6 months') AS window_start_mth,
      date(m3.mth, '+5 months') AS window_end_mth
    FROM monthly_product_sales m3
  ) w
    ON w.product_id = m.product_id
    AND w.target_mth = m.mth
  LEFT JOIN monthly_product_sales s
    ON s.product_id = m.product_id
    AND s.mth >= w.window_start_mth
    AND s.mth <= w.window_end_mth
  GROUP BY
    m.product_id,
    m.mth,
    w.window_type,
    w.window_start_mth,
    w.window_end_mth
),
cma_per_product_month AS (
  SELECT
    w_left.product_id,
    w_left.target_mth,
    (COALESCE(w_left.window_qty_sum,0) + COALESCE(w_right.window_qty_sum,0)) * 1.0
      / ( (CASE WHEN w_left.window_months_count IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE w_left.window_months_count END)
          + (CASE WHEN w_right.window_months_count IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE w_right.window_months_count END)
        ) AS cma
  FROM product_12m_centered_moving_avg_windows w_left
  JOIN product_12m_centered_moving_avg_windows w_right
    ON w_left.product_id = w_right.product_id
    AND w_left.target_mth = w_right.target_mth
    AND w_left.window_type = 'left5_right6'
    AND w_right.window_type = 'left6_right5'
),
products_all_months_ratio_above_2 AS (
  SELECT
    m.product_id
  FROM monthly_product_sales m
  JOIN cma_per_product_month c
    ON c.product_id = m.product_id
    AND c.target_mth = m.mth
  WHERE m.mth BETWEEN '2017-01-01' AND '2017-12-01'

  GROUP BY m.product_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) = 12
),
detailed_month_ratios AS (
  SELECT
    m.product_id,
    p.name AS product_name,
    m.mth AS month,
    CAST(m.qty AS REAL) / c.cma AS sales_to_cma_ratio
  FROM monthly_product_sales m
  JOIN cma_per_product_month c
    ON c.product_id = m.product_id
    AND c.target_mth = m.mth
  JOIN products p ON p.id = m.product_id
  WHERE m.mth BETWEEN '2017-01-01' AND '2017-12-01'
)

  dm.month,
  dm.sales_to_cma_ratio,

FROM products p
LEFT JOIN products_all_months_ratio_above_2 ok ON ok.product_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN detailed_month_ratios dm ON dm.product_id = p.id
WHERE ok.product_id IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY p.id, dm.month

rows.question: Based on our customer pizza order information, summarize the total quantity of each ingredient used in the pizzas we delivered. Output the name and quantity for each ingredient.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH delivered_customer_orders AS (
  SELECT order_id, customer_id, pizza_id, order_time
  FROM pizza_clean_customer_orders
),
pizza_recipe_topping_rows AS (
  -- parse comma-separated topping ids into rows; ignore null/empty
  SELECT
    CAST(pizza_id AS INTEGER) AS pizza_id,
    CAST(trim(value) AS INTEGER) AS topping_id
  FROM pizza_recipes,
    json_each(
      CASE
        WHEN toppings IS NULL THEN '[]'
        WHEN trim(toppings) = '' THEN '[]'
        ELSE json('[' || replace(toppings, ' ', '') || ']')
      END
    )
  WHERE toppings IS NOT NULL AND trim(toppings) <> ''
),
order_extra_toppings AS (
  -- sum extras_count per order and topping id; exclude null extras
  SELECT
    order_id,
    CAST(extras AS INTEGER) AS topping_id,
    SUM(extras_count) AS extras_count_sum
  FROM pizza_get_extras
  WHERE extras IS NOT NULL AND trim(CAST(extras AS TEXT)) <> ''
  GROUP BY order_id, CAST(extras AS INTEGER)
),
-- base counts: one per delivered order per topping from the recipe (count is occurrences in recipe per pizza)
base_per_order_topping AS (
  SELECT
    dco.order_id,
    prtr.topping_id,
    COUNT(*) AS base_count
  FROM delivered_customer_orders dco
  JOIN pizza_recipe_topping_rows prtr
    ON dco.pizza_id = prtr.pizza_id
  GROUP BY dco.order_id, prtr.topping_id
),
-- extras limited to delivered orders
extras_per_order_topping AS (
  SELECT oet.order_id, oet.topping_id, oet.extras_count_sum
  FROM order_extra_toppings oet
  JOIN delivered_customer_orders dco ON dco.order_id = oet.order_id
),
-- combine base and extras per order+topping
combined_per_order_topping AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(b.order_id, e.order_id) AS order_id,
    COALESCE(b.topping_id, e.topping_id) AS topping_id,
    COALESCE(b.base_count, 0) + COALESCE(e.extras_count_sum, 0) AS total_count_for_order_topping
  FROM base_per_order_topping b
  LEFT JOIN extras_per_order_topping e
    ON b.order_id = e.order_id AND b.topping_id = e.topping_id
  UNION
  -- include extras that have no base entry for that order+topping
  SELECT
    e.order_id,
    e.topping_id,
    COALESCE(e.extras_count_sum, 0)
  FROM extras_per_order_topping e
  LEFT JOIN base_per_order_topping b
    ON b.order_id = e.order_id AND b.topping_id = e.topping_id
  WHERE b.order_id IS NULL
)
SELECT
  pt.topping_name AS topping_name,
  SUM(c.total_count_for_order_topping) AS total_quantity
FROM combined_per_order_topping c
JOIN pizza_toppings pt
  ON pt.topping_id = c.topping_id
WHERE pt.topping_name IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY pt.topping_name
ORDER BY total_quantity DESC, topping_name ASC

rows.question: Calculate the total income from Meat Lovers pizzas priced at $12 and Vegetarian pizzas at $10. Include any extra toppings charged at $1 each. Ensure that canceled orders are filtered out. How much money has Pizza Runner earned in total?

    ) AS extras_text
  FROM pizza_customer_orders pco

  LEFT JOIN pizza_clean_runner_orders pcr USING(order_id)

),
orders_with_pizza_name AS (

rows.question: Identify the first 10 words, sorted alphabetically, that are 4 to 5 characters long, start with 'r', and have at least one anagram of the same length, considering case-sensitive letters. Provide the count of such anagrams for each word.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH trimmed AS (
  SELECT words AS word, TRIM(words) AS w, LENGTH(TRIM(words)) AS len
  FROM word_list
  WHERE words IS NOT NULL
),
nums(i) AS (
  VALUES (1),(2),(3),(4),(5)
),
letters AS (
  SELECT t.word, t.w, t.len,
         SUBSTR(t.w, nums.i, 1) AS ch
  FROM trimmed t
  JOIN nums ON nums.i <= t.len
),
sorted_letters AS (
  SELECT word, w, len,
    (SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(ch, '')
     FROM (
       SELECT ch FROM letters l2
       WHERE l2.word = l1.word
         AND ch IS NOT NULL AND ch <> ''
       ORDER BY ch
     )
    ) AS sorted
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT word, w, len FROM letters) l1
),
groups AS (
  SELECT sorted, len, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM sorted_letters
  GROUP BY sorted, len
  HAVING cnt > 1
)
SELECT s.word AS word, s.len AS length, g.cnt - 1 AS anagram_count
FROM sorted_letters s
JOIN groups g ON s.sorted = g.sorted AND s.len = g.len
WHERE s.len IN (4,5)
  AND s.w LIKE 'r%'
ORDER BY s.word ASC
LIMIT 10

rows.question: Could you find out the average percentage of the total lifetime sales (LTV) that occur in the first 7 and 30 days after a customer's initial purchase?   FROM costs

sale_costs AS (

  FROM dec_sales ds
  LEFT JOIN cost_pref cp
    ON ds.prod_id = cp.prod_id
   AND ds.time_id = cp.time_id
   AND ds.channel_id = cp.channel_id
   AND ds.promo_id = cp.promo_id
  LEFT JOIN cost_fallback cf
    ON ds.prod_id = cf.prod_id
   AND ds.time_id = cf.time_id
),

cust_profit AS (
  SELECT sc.cust_id,
         SUM(sc.amount_sold) AS total_amount_sold,
         SUM(sc.quantity_sold * sc.unit_cost_used) AS total_cost,
         SUM(sc.amount_sold) - SUM(sc.quantity_sold * sc.unit_cost_used) AS profit
  FROM sale_costs sc
  GROUP BY sc.cust_id
),

cust_counts AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_customers
  FROM cust_profit

  SELECT cp.cust_id,

         (SELECT total_customers FROM cust_counts) AS total_customers,
         (SELECT base_size FROM decile_sizes) AS base_size,

      CASE
        WHEN m.home_team_api_id = t.team_api_id AND m.home_team_goal IS NOT NULL THEN m.home_team_goal
        WHEN m.away_team_api_id = t.team_api_id AND m.away_team_goal IS NOT NULL THEN m.away_team_goal
        ELSE 0

    ON m.home_team_api_id = t.team_api_id OR m.away_team_api_id = t.team_api_id

  GROUP BY team_api_id
),
counts AS (

),

  FROM team_max_season_goals

  SELECT
    user_id,
    CASE
      WHEN birth_date IS NULL THEN NULL

      WHEN substr(birth_date,5,1) = '-' AND substr(birth_date,8,1) = '-' AND length(birth_date) >= 10

      WHEN instr(birth_date,'/') > 0 AND length(birth_date) >= 8

      WHEN length(birth_date) = 8 AND birth_date GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]'
           AND date(substr(birth_date,1,4) || '-' || substr(birth_date,5,2) || '-' || substr(birth_date,7,2)) IS NOT NULL

    (SELECT AVG(predicted_daily_order_item_count) FROM predictions

    ) AS ma_2018_12_08

rows.question: What is the distance of the longest route where Abakan is either the departure or destination city (in kilometers)?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH f AS (
  SELECT
    fl.*,
    dep.city AS dep_city,
    dep.coordinates AS dep_coordinates,
    arr.city AS arr_city,
    arr.coordinates AS arr_coordinates
  FROM flights fl
  JOIN airports_data dep ON fl.departure_airport = dep.airport_code
  JOIN airports_data arr ON fl.arrival_airport = arr.airport_code
  WHERE (dep.city->>'en' = 'Abakan' OR arr.city->>'en' = 'Abakan')
    AND dep.coordinates IS NOT NULL
    AND arr.coordinates IS NOT NULL
),
coords AS (
  SELECT
    *,
    -- extract lon,lat numeric values from point text like "(lon,lat)"
    CAST(TRIM(SUBSTR(dep_coordinates, 2, INSTR(dep_coordinates, ',')-2)) AS REAL) AS dep_lon,
    CAST(TRIM(SUBSTR(dep_coordinates, INSTR(dep_coordinates, ',')+1, LENGTH(dep_coordinates)-INSTR(dep_coordinates, ',')-1)) AS REAL) AS dep_lat,
    CAST(TRIM(SUBSTR(arr_coordinates, 2, INSTR(arr_coordinates, ',')-2)) AS REAL) AS arr_lon,
    CAST(TRIM(SUBSTR(arr_coordinates, INSTR(arr_coordinates, ',')+1, LENGTH(arr_coordinates)-INSTR(arr_coordinates, ',')-1)) AS REAL) AS arr_lat
  FROM f
),
distances AS (
  SELECT
    *,
    2.0 * 6371.0 * ASIN(
      SQRT(
        POWER(SIN(RADIANS((arr_lat - dep_lat) / 2.0)), 2)
        + COS(RADIANS(dep_lat)) * COS(RADIANS(arr_lat)) * POWER(SIN(RADIANS((arr_lon - dep_lon) / 2.0)), 2)
      )
    ) AS distance_km,
    CASE WHEN dep_city->>'en' = 'Abakan' THEN departure_airport ELSE arrival_airport END AS departure_airport_code,
    CASE WHEN dep_city->>'en' = 'Abakan' THEN arrival_airport ELSE departure_airport END AS arrival_airport_code,
    CASE WHEN dep_city->>'en' = 'Abakan' THEN dep_city->>'en' ELSE arr_city->>'en' END AS departure_city_en,
    CASE WHEN dep_city->>'en' = 'Abakan' THEN arr_city->>'en' ELSE dep_city->>'en' END AS arrival_city_en
  FROM coords
)
SELECT
  ROUND(distance_km, 3) AS max_distance_km,
  departure_airport_code AS departure_airport_code,
  arrival_airport_code AS arrival_airport_code,
  departure_city_en AS departure_city_en,
  arrival_city_en AS arrival_city_en,
  flight_id
FROM distances
ORDER BY distance_km DESC
LIMIT 1

rows.question: Distribute all the unique city pairs into the distance ranges 0, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000, and 6000+, based on their average distance of all routes between them. Then how many pairs are there in the distance range with the fewest unique city paires?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH airports_core AS (
SELECT
  airport_code,
  json_extract(city, '$.en') AS city_en,
  CAST(substr(trim('(' || replace(replace(coordinates, '(', ''), ')', '') || ')'), 1,
       instr(replace(replace(coordinates, '(', ''), ')', ''), ',') - 1) AS REAL) AS longitude,
  CAST(trim(substr(replace(replace(coordinates, '(', ''), ')', ''), instr(replace(replace(coordinates, '(', ''), ')', ''), ',') + 1)) AS REAL) AS latitude,
  timezone
FROM airports_data
),
flights_with_airport_cities_and_coords AS (
SELECT
  f.flight_id,
  f.flight_no,
  f.scheduled_departure,
  f.scheduled_arrival,
  f.departure_airport,
  f.arrival_airport,
  dep.city_en AS dep_city_en,
  arr.city_en AS arr_city_en,
  dep.longitude AS dep_longitude,
  dep.latitude AS dep_latitude,
  arr.longitude AS arr_longitude,
  arr.latitude AS arr_latitude,
  f.status,
  f.aircraft_code
FROM flights f
LEFT JOIN airports_core dep ON f.departure_airport = dep.airport_code
LEFT JOIN airports_core arr ON f.arrival_airport = arr.airport_code
WHERE f.departure_airport IS NOT NULL
  AND f.arrival_airport IS NOT NULL
),
unordered_city_pairs_flight_distances AS (
SELECT
  f.flight_id,
  CASE WHEN f.dep_city_en <= f.arr_city_en THEN f.dep_city_en ELSE f.arr_city_en END AS city_a,
  CASE WHEN f.dep_city_en <= f.arr_city_en THEN f.arr_city_en ELSE f.dep_city_en END AS city_b,
  -- great-circle distance (Haversine) in kilometers between departure and arrival coordinates
  ( 
    6371.0 * 2.0 * 
    ASIN(
      MIN(1.0, 
        SQRT(
          POWER(SIN(RADIANS((f.arr_latitude - f.dep_latitude) / 2.0)), 2)
          + COS(RADIANS(f.dep_latitude)) * COS(RADIANS(f.arr_latitude))
          * POWER(SIN(RADIANS((f.arr_longitude - f.dep_longitude) / 2.0)), 2)
        )
      )
    )
  ) AS distance_km
FROM flights_with_airport_cities_and_coords f
WHERE f.dep_city_en IS NOT NULL
  AND f.arr_city_en IS NOT NULL
  AND f.dep_city_en != f.arr_city_en
)
SELECT
  b.bucket_label,
  b.pair_count,
  m.min_bucket_label,
  m.min_pair_count
FROM (
  -- counts per bucket
  SELECT
    bucket_label,
    COUNT(*) AS pair_count
  FROM (
    -- average distance per unordered city pair
    SELECT
      city_a,
      city_b,
      AVG(distance_km) AS avg_km,
      CASE
        WHEN AVG(distance_km) < 1000 THEN '0'
        WHEN AVG(distance_km) < 2000 THEN '1000'
        WHEN AVG(distance_km) < 3000 THEN '2000'
        WHEN AVG(distance_km) < 4000 THEN '3000'
        WHEN AVG(distance_km) < 5000 THEN '4000'
        WHEN AVG(distance_km) < 6000 THEN '5000'
        ELSE '6000+'
      END AS bucket_label
    FROM unordered_city_pairs_flight_distances
    WHERE city_a IS NOT NULL
      AND city_b IS NOT NULL
      AND city_a <> city_b
    GROUP BY city_a, city_b
  ) avg_pairs
  GROUP BY bucket_label
) b
CROSS JOIN (
  -- identify minimum bucket
  SELECT bucket_label AS min_bucket_label, pair_count AS min_pair_count
  FROM (
    SELECT
      CASE
        WHEN avg_km < 1000 THEN '0'
        WHEN avg_km < 2000 THEN '1000'
        WHEN avg_km < 3000 THEN '2000'
        WHEN avg_km < 4000 THEN '3000'
        WHEN avg_km < 5000 THEN '4000'
        WHEN avg_km < 6000 THEN '5000'
        ELSE '6000+'
      END AS bucket_label,
      COUNT(*) AS pair_count
    FROM (
      SELECT city_a, city_b, AVG(distance_km) AS avg_km
      FROM unordered_city_pairs_flight_distances
      WHERE city_a IS NOT NULL
        AND city_b IS NOT NULL
        AND city_a <> city_b
      GROUP BY city_a, city_b
    ) t
    GROUP BY bucket_label
    ORDER BY pair_count ASC
    LIMIT 1
  ) s
) m
ORDER BY
  CASE b.bucket_label
    WHEN '0' THEN 0
    WHEN '1000' THEN 1
    WHEN '2000' THEN 2
    WHEN '3000' THEN 3
    WHEN '4000' THEN 4
    WHEN '5000' THEN 5
    WHEN '6000+' THEN 6
    ELSE 7
  END

          -- MM:SS
          CAST(substr(Matches.duration, 1, instr(Matches.duration, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60
          + CAST(substr(Matches.duration, instr(Matches.duration, ':') + 1) AS INTEGER)
        )
      WHEN Matches.duration LIKE '%:%' AND (LENGTH(Matches.duration) - LENGTH(REPLACE(Matches.duration, ':', ''))) = 2
        THEN (
          -- H:MM:SS or HH:MM:SS
          CAST(substr(Matches.duration, 1, instr(Matches.duration, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 3600
          + CAST(
              substr(
                Matches.duration,
                instr(Matches.duration, ':') + 1,
                instr(substr(Matches.duration, instr(Matches.duration, ':') + 1), ':') - 1
              ) AS INTEGER
            ) * 60
          + CAST(
              substr(
                Matches.duration,
                instr(Matches.duration, ':') + 1 + instr(substr(Matches.duration, instr(Matches.duration, ':') + 1), ':')
              ) AS INTEGER
            )
        )
      ELSE NULL
    END AS duration_seconds
  FROM Matches
  WHERE Matches.duration IS NOT NULL AND Matches.duration != ''
)
SELECT
  mwtad.winner_name AS winner_name,
  mwtad.loser_name AS loser_name,
  mwtad.match_id AS match_id,
  mwtad.duration AS duration,
  mwtad.title_id AS belt_id
FROM matches_with_titles_and_durations mwtad
JOIN normalized_match_durations nmd ON nmd.match_id = mwtad.match_id
WHERE mwtad.title_name = 'NXT'
  AND mwtad.title_change = 0
  AND nmd.duration_seconds IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY nmd.duration_seconds ASC, mwtad.match_id ASC
LIMIT 1

rows.question: List the bowlers (including their ID, first name, and last name), match number, game number, handicap score, tournament date, and location for only those bowlers who have won games with a handicap score of 190 or less at all three venues: Thunderbird Lanes, Totem Lanes, and Bolero Lanes. Only include the specific game records where they won with a handicap score of 190 or less at these three locations.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH bowler_game_with_tourney_context AS (
  SELECT
    bs.BowlerID,
    b.BowlerFirstName,
    b.BowlerLastName,
    bs.MatchID,
    bs.GameNumber,
    bs.HandiCapScore,
    bs.WonGame,
    tm.TourneyID,
    t.TourneyDate,
    t.TourneyLocation
  FROM Bowler_Scores AS bs
  JOIN Bowlers AS b ON bs.BowlerID = b.BowlerID
  JOIN Tourney_Matches AS tm ON bs.MatchID = tm.MatchID
  JOIN Tournaments AS t ON tm.TourneyID = t.TourneyID
)
SELECT 
    bgw.BowlerID,
    bgw.BowlerFirstName,
    bgw.BowlerLastName,
    bgw.MatchID,
    bgw.GameNumber,
    bgw.HandiCapScore,
    bgw.TourneyDate,
    bgw.TourneyLocation
FROM bowler_game_with_tourney_context AS bgw
WHERE 
    bgw.WonGame = 1
    AND bgw.HandiCapScore <= 190
    AND bgw.TourneyLocation IN ('Thunderbird Lanes','Totem Lanes','Bolero Lanes')
    AND bgw.BowlerID IN (
        SELECT BowlerID
        FROM bowler_game_with_tourney_context
        WHERE WonGame = 1
          AND HandiCapScore <= 190
          AND TourneyLocation IN ('Thunderbird Lanes','Totem Lanes','Bolero Lanes')
        GROUP BY BowlerID
        HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT TourneyLocation) = 3
    )
ORDER BY 
    bgw.BowlerID ASC,
    bgw.TourneyDate ASC,
    bgw.MatchID ASC,
    bgw.GameNumber ASC

rows.question: Could you provide a list of last names for all students who have completed English courses (where completion is defined as having a ClassStatus of 2), along with their quintile ranks based on their individual grades in those courses? The quintile should be determined by calculating how many students have grades greater than or equal to each student's grade, then dividing this ranking by the total number of students who completed English courses. The quintiles should be labeled as "First" (top 20%), "Second" (top 21-40%), "Third" (top 41-60%), "Fourth" (top 61-80%), and "Fifth" (bottom 20%). Please sort the results from highest performing quintile to lowest (First to Fifth).
rows.pred_sql:
WITH student_course_completions AS (
  SELECT
    ss.StudentID,
    ss.ClassID,
    ss.ClassStatus,
    ss.Grade,
    st.StudLastName,
    cl.SubjectID,
    subj.CategoryID,
    cat.CategoryDescription
  FROM Student_Schedules ss
  JOIN Students st ON ss.StudentID = st.StudentID
  JOIN Classes cl ON ss.ClassID = cl.ClassID
  JOIN Subjects subj ON cl.SubjectID = subj.SubjectID
  JOIN Categories cat ON subj.CategoryID = cat.CategoryID
  WHERE ss.ClassStatus IS NOT NULL
),
student_completed_category_grades AS (
  SELECT
    scc.StudentID,
    scc.StudLastName,
    scc.ClassID,
    scc.Grade,
    scc.CategoryID,
    scc.CategoryDescription
  FROM student_course_completions scc
  WHERE scc.ClassStatus = 2
),
student_completed_category_rank_prep AS (
  SELECT
    sc.StudentID,
    sc.StudLastName,
    sc.ClassID,
    sc.Grade,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) 
       FROM student_completed_category_grades sc2
       WHERE sc2.CategoryID = sc.CategoryID
         AND sc2.Grade >= sc.Grade
    ) AS RankGe_Count,
    sc.CategoryID,
    sc.CategoryDescription,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) 
       FROM student_completed_category_grades sc3
       WHERE sc3.CategoryID = sc.CategoryID
    ) AS TotalCompletedInCategory
  FROM student_completed_category_grades sc
)
SELECT
  StudLastName,
  CASE
    WHEN (RankGe_Count * 1.0) / TotalCompletedInCategory <= 0.20 THEN 'First'
    WHEN (RankGe_Count * 1.0) / TotalCompletedInCategory <= 0.40 THEN 'Second'
    WHEN (RankGe_Count * 1.0) / TotalCompletedInCategory <= 0.60 THEN 'Third'
    WHEN (RankGe_Count * 1.0) / TotalCompletedInCategory <= 0.80 THEN 'Fourth'
    ELSE 'Fifth'
  END AS QuintileLabel
FROM student_completed_category_rank_prep
WHERE CategoryDescription = 'English'
  AND RankGe_Count IS NOT NULL
  AND TotalCompletedInCategory IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY
  CASE
    WHEN (RankGe_Count * 1.0) / TotalCompletedInCategory <= 0.20 THEN 1
    WHEN (RankGe_Count * 1.0) / TotalCompletedInCategory <= 0.40 THEN 2
    WHEN (RankGe_Count * 1.0) / TotalCompletedInCategory <= 0.60 THEN 3
    WHEN (RankGe_Count * 1.0) / TotalCompletedInCategory <= 0.80 THEN 4
    ELSE 5
  END

rows.question: How did each salesperson's annual total sales compare to their annual sales quota? Provide the difference between their total sales and the quota for each year, organized by salesperson and year.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH sales_by_person_year AS (
  SELECT
    salespersonid AS salesperson_id,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', orderdate) AS INTEGER) AS year,
    SUM(totaldue) AS total_sales
  FROM salesorderheader
  WHERE salespersonid IS NOT NULL AND orderdate IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY salespersonid, CAST(strftime('%Y', orderdate) AS INTEGER)
),
quota_by_person_year AS (
  SELECT
    BusinessEntityID AS salesperson_id,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', QuotaDate) AS INTEGER) AS year,
    SUM(SalesQuota) AS sales_quota
  FROM SalesPersonQuotaHistory
  WHERE SalesQuota IS NOT NULL AND QuotaDate IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY BusinessEntityID, CAST(strftime('%Y', QuotaDate) AS INTEGER)
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(s.salesperson_id, q.salesperson_id) AS salesperson_id,
  COALESCE(s.year, q.year) AS year,
  COALESCE(s.total_sales, 0.0) AS total_sales,
  COALESCE(q.sales_quota, 0.0) AS sales_quota,
  COALESCE(s.total_sales, 0.0) - COALESCE(q.sales_quota, 0.0) AS difference
FROM sales_by_person_year s
LEFT JOIN quota_by_person_year q
  ON s.salesperson_id = q.salesperson_id AND s.year = q.year
UNION
SELECT
  COALESCE(s.salesperson_id, q.salesperson_id) AS salesperson_id,
  COALESCE(s.year, q.year) AS year,
  COALESCE(s.total_sales, 0.0) AS total_sales,
  COALESCE(q.sales_quota, 0.0) AS sales_quota,
  COALESCE(s.total_sales, 0.0) - COALESCE(q.sales_quota, 0.0) AS difference
FROM sales_by_person_year s
RIGHT JOIN quota_by_person_year q
  ON s.salesperson_id = q.salesperson_id AND s.year = q.year
ORDER BY salesperson_id ASC, year ASC

rows.question: Calculate the duration of each track, classify them as short, medium, or long, output the minimum and maximum time for each kind (in minutes) and the total revenue for each category, group by the category.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH track_basic AS (
  SELECT
    t.TrackId,
    t.Milliseconds,
    (t.Milliseconds / 60000.0) AS DurationMinutes,
    t.UnitPrice AS TrackUnitPrice
  FROM Track t
  WHERE t.TrackId IS NOT NULL
    AND t.Milliseconds IS NOT NULL
),
track_invoice_lines AS (
  -- only invoice lines that reference an existing track will join below,
  -- keep InvoiceLine.UnitPrice and Quantity for revenue calc
  SELECT
    il.InvoiceLineId,
    il.TrackId,
    il.Quantity,
    il.UnitPrice AS InvoiceLineUnitPrice
  FROM InvoiceLine il
),
stats AS (
  SELECT
    MIN(tb.Milliseconds) AS MIN_ms,
    AVG(tb.Milliseconds) AS AVG_ms,
    MAX(tb.Milliseconds) AS MAX_ms,
    (MIN(tb.Milliseconds) + AVG(tb.Milliseconds)) / 2.0 AS midpoint1_ms,
    (AVG(tb.Milliseconds) + MAX(tb.Milliseconds)) / 2.0 AS midpoint2_ms
  FROM track_basic tb
)
SELECT
  c.category AS Category,
  MIN(tb.DurationMinutes) AS MinDurationMinutes,
  MAX(tb.DurationMinutes) AS MaxDurationMinutes,
  -- revenue: for each invoice line use its UnitPrice * Quantity; if a track has no invoice lines it contributes 0
  SUM(COALESCE(il.InvoiceLineUnitPrice, 0) * COALESCE(il.Quantity, 0)) AS TotalRevenue
FROM track_basic tb
CROSS JOIN stats s
LEFT JOIN track_invoice_lines il
  ON il.TrackId = tb.TrackId
-- assign category by milliseconds using the computed midpoints
JOIN (
  SELECT 'short' AS category UNION ALL SELECT 'medium' UNION ALL SELECT 'long'
) c ON (
     (c.category = 'short'  AND tb.Milliseconds >= s.MIN_ms      AND tb.Milliseconds <  s.midpoint1_ms)
  OR (c.category = 'medium' AND tb.Milliseconds >= s.midpoint1_ms AND tb.Milliseconds <  s.midpoint2_ms)
  OR (c.category = 'long'   AND tb.Milliseconds >= s.midpoint2_ms AND tb.Milliseconds <= s.MAX_ms)
)
GROUP BY c.category
ORDER BY CASE c.category WHEN 'short' THEN 1 WHEN 'medium' THEN 2 WHEN 'long' THEN 3 END

rows.question: Prepare a comprehensive performance report on our sellers, focusing on total sales, average item price, average review scores, and packing times. Ensure that the report includes only those sellers who have sold a quantity of more than 100 products and highlight the product category names in English with the highest sales volume.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH order_items_enriched_by_product_and_seller AS (
  SELECT
    oi.order_id,
    oi.order_item_id,
    oi.seller_id,
    oi.product_id,
    oi.price,
    oi.freight_value,
    p.product_category_name
  FROM order_items AS oi
  LEFT JOIN products AS p
    ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
),
-- per seller+order aggregates (to avoid double counting when an order has multiple items for same seller)
seller_order_item_cohort AS (
  SELECT
    seller_id,
    order_id,
    COUNT(*) AS items_in_order_for_seller,
    SUM(price) AS sum_price_in_order_for_seller
  FROM order_items_enriched_by_product_and_seller
  GROUP BY seller_id, order_id
),
-- per seller total metrics from order_items (quantity and revenue)
seller_totals AS (
  SELECT
    seller_id,
    SUM(items_in_order_for_seller) AS total_quantity_sold,
    SUM(sum_price_in_order_for_seller) AS total_sales_revenue,
    CASE WHEN SUM(items_in_order_for_seller) = 0 THEN NULL
         ELSE SUM(sum_price_in_order_for_seller) * 1.0 / SUM(items_in_order_for_seller)
    END AS average_item_price
  FROM seller_order_item_cohort
  GROUP BY seller_id
),
-- per seller distinct-order average review_score (ignore NULLs)
seller_avg_review AS (
  SELECT
    soc.seller_id,
    AVG(orv.review_score) AS average_review_score
  FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT seller_id, order_id FROM seller_order_item_cohort
  ) AS soc
  JOIN order_reviews orv
    ON soc.order_id = orv.order_id
  WHERE orv.review_score IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY soc.seller_id
),
-- per seller distinct-order packing hours averaged (only orders with both timestamps)
seller_avg_packing AS (
  SELECT
    soc.seller_id,
    AVG(
      (CAST(strftime('%s', o.order_delivered_carrier_date) AS REAL)
       - CAST(strftime('%s', o.order_approved_at) AS REAL)
      ) / 3600.0
    ) AS average_packing_time_hours
  FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT seller_id, order_id FROM seller_order_item_cohort
  ) AS soc
  JOIN orders o
    ON soc.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.order_approved_at IS NOT NULL
    AND o.order_delivered_carrier_date IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY soc.seller_id
),
-- per seller per product category (original category) counts
seller_category_counts AS (
  SELECT
    oip.seller_id,
    oip.product_category_name,
    COUNT(1) AS category_quantity
  FROM order_items_enriched_by_product_and_seller oip
  GROUP BY oip.seller_id, oip.product_category_name
),
-- map to english category and pick top per seller; if multiple tie, pick one deterministically via MIN(product_category_name_english)
seller_top_category AS (
  SELECT
    scc.seller_id,
    pct.product_category_name_english AS top_product_category_english,
    scc.category_quantity AS top_product_category_quantity
  FROM seller_category_counts scc
  LEFT JOIN product_category_name_translation pct
    ON scc.product_category_name = pct.product_category_name
  WHERE scc.category_quantity = (
    SELECT MAX(category_quantity)
    FROM seller_category_counts scc2
    WHERE scc2.seller_id = scc.seller_id
  )
  -- In case of ties, choose the english name with smallest text (deterministic)
  ORDER BY scc.seller_id, top_product_category_quantity DESC, pct.product_category_name_english
),
-- reduce seller_top_category to one row per seller (tie-breaker applied by MIN)
seller_top_category_one AS (
  SELECT
    seller_id,
    MIN(top_product_category_english) AS top_product_category_english,
    MAX(top_product_category_quantity) AS top_product_category_quantity
  FROM seller_top_category
  GROUP BY seller_id
)
SELECT
  s.seller_id,
  st.total_sales_revenue,
  st.total_quantity_sold,
  st.average_item_price,
  sar.average_review_score,
  sap.average_packing_time_hours,
  stc.top_product_category_english,
  stc.top_product_category_quantity
FROM seller_totals st
JOIN sellers s
  ON s.seller_id = st.seller_id
LEFT JOIN seller_avg_review sar
  ON sar.seller_id = st.seller_id
LEFT JOIN seller_avg_packing sap
  ON sap.seller_id = st.seller_id
LEFT JOIN seller_top_category_one stc
  ON stc.seller_id = st.seller_id
WHERE st.total_quantity_sold > 100
ORDER BY st.total_sales_revenue DESC
